news.title: A look at Huawei and DeepSeek's mutual reliance, where Huawei provides compute hardware while DeepSeek contributes model workloads and kernel optimization (SemiAnalysis)
news.title_en: A look at Huawei and DeepSeek's mutual reliance, where Huawei provides compute hardware while DeepSeek contributes model workloads and kernel optimization (SemiAnalysis)
news.author: SemiAnalysis
news.article_content:
Neither can do this alone. Although they have Pangu, Huawei has no frontier lab to prove their chip can train or infer models, DeepSeek has models but cannot buy the compute it needs. Each supplies exactly what the other lacks: Huawei provides the hardware and native software stack; DeepSeek brings the workloads and engineering needed to make that hardware useful for its models. September 30’s release of Ascend support in DeepSeek repositories is an artifact of this trade, where the exchange runs through the kernel-authoring language.

Source: SemiAnalysis - Note that the diagram is a simulation.In 2028 or even 2027, DeepSeek will likely be primarily using Huawei’s stack, especially with the external and internal pressure to build a fully domestic chinese ecosystem. As we show here and in future articles, the Huawei ecosystem is already mature and well developed, with strong foundations from the Ascend time and DeepSeek engineers building further ontop.

In this article, we’ll first examine Ascend 950PR’s architecture and benchmark its compute and memory performance. We then explore DeepSeek’s software releases, from TileLang’s compiler capabilities to hardware-specific kernel optimizations and rack-scale communication. Finally, we analyze DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s execution profile.

We deep-dived into CANN and the Ascend 950 architecture in our DeepSeek V4 Pro article. Since then, more interesting details have been revealed.

Source: SemiAnalysisStarting from the chip, many variants of 950PR/DT have appeared with varying core counts, HBM stack height, and cache sizes. Some are likely either virtualised/simulated, or for testing only. This is because only a fraction of dies and HBM stacks meet the target spec, due to both outright defects and parametric shortfalls in power and performance, so Huawei bins both compute and memory into multiple SKUs and pairs weaker memory with weaker compute, rather than binning only compute as Nvidia does.

Source: SemiAnalysisThis isn’t new, 910B also has variants such as 910B1, 910B2, 910B3, 910B4. For the following microbenchmarks, we use an Ascend 950PR_9579, with 28 cube cores and 128 GiB HBM.

root@cb3bb851f93f:/workspace# npu-smi info
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| npu-smi 25.7.rc1.6                               Version: 25.7.rc1.6                            |
+--------+------------------+---------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
| NPU ID | Name             | Health        | Power(W)    Temp(C)           Hugepages-Usage(page) |
|        |                  | Bus-Id        | NPU Util(%) Memory-Usage(MB)  HBM-Usage(MB)         |
+========+==================+===============+=====================================================+
| 0      | Ascend950PR      | OK            | 203.3       56                0     / 0             |
|        |                  | 0000:12:00.0  | 0           0    / 0          5242  / 131072        |
+========+==================+===============+=====================================================+
+---------------------------+---------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
| NPU ID                    | Process id    | Process name             | Process memory(MB)       |
+===========================+===============+=====================================================+
| No running processes found in NPU 0                                                             |
+===========================+===============+=====================================================+Running point chases reading 16 KiB of integer payload per launch, it stays near 134ns through 18 blocks, rises to 182ns at 56, then jumps to 391ns at 64. This is consistent with a second wave beyond 56 Vector cores.

Source: SemiAnalysisThen by running a scalar pointer-chase probe separately on every Cube and Vector core, recording load timings at matching addresses throughout a 128 MiB chain, we get the following graph. Each cell’s color represents the mean absolute difference between two cores' address profiles, producing two groups that match the decoded dies.

Source: SemiAnalysisGoing further, by timing a Vector core’s pointer chase while another core runs either memory traffic or register-only work; the extra slowdown reveals which subsystems share resources, supporting groups such as {0,2,4} and {1,3,5}. Mixed Cube/Vector launches identify each subsystem’s one Cube and two Vectors, which we draw together within those groups, with physical positions remaining schematic.

Source: SemiAnalysisCPU within the NPUEach 950PR comes with a variable number of Linx816 AArch64 ELF AICPUs. The MIDR numbers imply these cores are likely the same as the middle cores in the Kirin 9000S/9010. These AICPU cores have instruction set:

fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid
asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop sha3 sm3 sm4 asimddp sha512 sve
asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb paca pacg dcpodp flagm2
frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh rng ecvFor this SKU, there are 7 configured, 6 visible, and 5 executing AICPU cores. Other than device control it can provide CPU-operator support, such as KV metadata. The AICPU helps out for short work where D2H overhead take up most of the time.

For DSA, a small scheduling step reads the current sequence lengths and assigns indexer work to accelerator cores. Cube/Vector cores then compute INT8 indexer scores and select the top 2,048 indices. These planning, index selection, and gather steps are ran on AICPUs in vLLM-ascend implementation, and we compare their performance to running on the host CPU.

Source: SemiAnalysisDue to their limited compute performance, AICPU is only good for short work where overhead dominates, and work where data starts and is consumed at the NPU.

Ascend 950PR is designed for prefill and recommendation. It gets lower memory bandwidth and core than its bigger brother the 950DT.

The results below are not from DeepSeek’s contributions but from stock torch.matmul on ascend resolving to aclnnMatmul_MatMulV3Common_MatMulV3. We compared 1,055 BF16 GEMM shapes from several open-sourced models. Huawei’s best kernels hits 99.7% of the ceiling, showing DeepSeek’s 99+% from DeepGEMM isn’t the only way to maximize utilization. Huawei engineers did good work too.

Source: SemiAnalysisThe advantage is concentrated in compute-bound work. On the shapes below Ascend’s ridge, its median achieved/attainable fraction is 41.5% versus H100’s 46.8%. Some of Nvidia’s results were power-limited and did not hit maximum SM clock: median power around 690-698 W out of a 700 W limit, and median sampled SM clocks at 1335-1470 MHz, below the max of 1830 MHz. Huawei approximated 599-600 W, at 1500-1550 MHz against its 1650 MHz reference.

Ascend’s MXU design may contribute to some of this high utilization, Ascend stages matrix operands in dedicated L0A/L0B buffers and accumulators in L0C, with overlapping movement, computation and result handling. Huawei associates the enlarged L0C with more flexible tiling and reuse.

But of course, 950PR’s falls behind on absolute values, sitting somewhere between A100 and MI300X.

Source: SemiAnalysisMemBWMeasuring HBM memory bandwidth, we see 950PR’s effective bandwidth and bandwidth utilization surpassing H100 at small message size per buffers, and nearly matching H100 in bandwidth utilization at large message sizes.

Source: SemiAnalysisA dip appears in the curve as Ascend switches copy methods to a Vector-core TensorMove kernel that has more startup cost, so a slightly larger copy suddenly takes longer. For very large copies, that extra cost becomes relatively small, so bandwidth rises again.

Note that high FLOPs utilization and bandwidth utilization does not necessarily translate to high MFU/MBU. Training, especially with FSDP, requires collectives, checkpointing, and data moving that can be hard to overlap.

As we mentioned in our Jalepeno article, a “chip” in benchmarks is just a social construct. Multiple dies can be glue to form a bigger “chip”.  Thus performance per watt or TCO is the best comparison. But for China, watts are far cheaper. We’ll analyze Ascend’s perf per TCO in a future article.

OpenAI Jalapeño: Better Than Nvidia BlackwellBryan Shan, Myron Xie, and 4 others·Aug 25Read full storyHardware raises the ceiling, but software lets you reach that ceiling. Although Huawei’s hardware may be beyond ~5 years behind(compared to A100), the software is right at the frontier.

For the 6 repos that received ascend support(TileLang, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, FlashMLA, DeepSelect), only TileLang is usable as of writing, and CANN 9.2.0 has not been released. Deepseek requires CANN 9.2.0 which was released after time of writing, and a C++20 compiler is required which CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 does not provide. The HDK will be released on Oct 15. This comes after DeepSeek’s open source week in 2025, where some of these repositories were released with Nvidia support only.

From the results above, we can see Huawei can already execute operations well; the symbiosis is about making the rest of the application & the work required to support it more efficient and reusable.

Huawei’s architecture is already influencing how DeepSeek’s software organizes data. Earlier FlashMLA KV-cache layouts stored quantized values and their scaling factors in separate regions. On Ascend, fetching a token then required separate transfers for its values and scales. The new implementation places them together, reducing the number of transfer requests by the memory transfer engine(MTE).

Source: SemiAnalysisFrom fast kernels to reusable kernel engineeringAscend 950 backend is merged into the main TileLang repository, rather than existing only in a separate Huawei adapter. It adds native compilation, scheduling, synchronization and runtime integration for Ascend’s execution model.

TileLang makes Ascend kernels easier to write, but developers still need to account for the hardware. They choose the calculations, tile sizes and where data is stored. The compiler handles much of the coordination between Cube cores, Vector cores and data transfers.

Digging below the implementation and looking at its performance against CANN and Triton-ascend, it can match and beat CANN at certain cases; the preferred implementation changes with size.  This is a warm-cache simple and naive benchmark.

Source: SemiAnalysisAutoSchedule uses data dependencies and estimated execution times to plan which operations can overlap. It also chooses how many buffer slots to use within the available on-chip memory, allowing upcoming data to load while the current tile is being processed. Developers can guide these decisions when the default schedule is not suitable.

news.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
news.title_en: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.

What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning.

Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind.

news.title: Anthropic takes on Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots with its always-on agent "Claude Duet"
news.title_en: Anthropic takes on Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots with its always-on agent "Claude Duet"
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that handles tasks on its own, even when the user is offline. The app is built on Claude Opus 5.5 and connects to services like Gmail, Slack, and Stripe through more than 6,000 connectors. It asks for approval before sensitive actions like payments. With Duet, Anthropic is responding to similar products from xAI, Meta, and OpenAI.

news.author: Bloomberg

Pressure to back promising AI startups is upending the VC investment process, with investors willing to buy into the same round at rapidly escalating valuations  —  Venture capitalists are fighting to invest in AI startup Emulate, driving its valuation
news.content_snippet: Venture capitalists are fighting to invest in AI startup Emulate, driving its valuation into the billions …
news.summary_en: Intense competition to back elite AI startups is upending traditional venture capital practices, with investors willingly entering the same funding round at escalating valuations. Driven by severe FOMO over missing the next foundational tech giant, VCs are aggressively bidding against each other for startups like Emulate, sidelining standard due diligence.
news.title_zh: AI投资狂热打破风投规则 同轮次估值遭疯狂追高

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 全球风险投资机构近期在面对如Emulate等头部AI初创团队时，彻底打破了传统尽调与定价流程。多位投资人为挤进热门项目的同一轮融资，不惜在几天甚至几小时内主动接受层层加价的超高估值。这种恐慌性争抢源于机构对错失下一代平台级AI巨头的极度焦虑，导致原有的投资纪律在算力与模型叙事面前全面失效。

news.content_snippet: The billionaire told Meta's board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.

									Apple must open iPhone to alternative app stores in Australia after Epic Games ruling				
				
											
													
						Marcus Mendes | Oct 21 2026 - 8:57 pm PT																
							
																1 Comment							
						
									
			
		
		
			
				
					


	
	

An Australian federal judge has ordered Apple to make sweeping changes to its App Store rules following a years-long antitrust battle with Epic Games. Apple has confirmed that it plans to appeal. Here are the details.

Apple must allow iPhone users with Australian Apple Accounts to install apps from third-party app stores and websites starting March 1, 2027, a federal judge ordered today in a 235-page decision. Apple has until February 15 to request an extension until May 3, 2027, subject to court approval.

Today’s order follows a ruling last year that Apple violated Australian competition law by restricting alternative app distribution and payment methods, in a lawsuit brought by Epic Games similar to its long-running legal battle with Apple in the US.

In his decision, Justice Jonathan Beach said Apple held “a substantial degree of power in the iOS app distribution services market and the iOS in-app payment solutions market,” and used its developer agreements and App Store guidelines to restrict competition.

The ruling also cited Apple’s actions against Epic Games in 2020, including its refusal to allow Epic Direct Pay, Fortnite’s removal from the App Store, and the subsequent termination of Epic’s developer account.

Justice Beach described the latter two actions as “a paradigm example of Apple’s enforcement of its restrictive terms, in contravention of” section 46 of Australia’s Competition and Consumer Act 2010, which prohibits corporations with substantial market power from engaging in conduct that has “the purpose, or has or is likely to have the effect, of substantially lessening competition” in that market.

As a result, Justice Beach issued a wide-ranging series of orders requiring Apple to, among other things:

The decision also addresses several other aspects of Apple’s App Store policies, including restrictions on its ability to turn off apps installed outside the App Store and requirements related to notarization.

The court also prohibited Apple from requiring developers to report transactions processed through alternative payment providers or offer Apple’s payment system alongside their preferred alternatives, both of which are requirements the company imposes in other regions, including Brazil and Japan.

When it comes to Apple’s wins in the decision, the list is much slimmer. Judge Beach rejected Epic’s request to extend the court’s injunctions worldwide and allowed Apple to maintain security scanning and notarization requirements for apps distributed outside the App Store. And while Apple must permit competing app marketplaces on iOS, it is not required to distribute them through its own App Store. This is a distinction he had already established in last year’s ruling.

Finally, the court ordered Apple to pay 85% of Epic’s legal costs incurred through the original trial, while reserving a decision on costs associated with the subsequent hearings over remedies.

Commenting on the decision, Epic confirmed “Fortnite is coming back to the App Store in Australia tomorrow,” and celebrated it as “great news for developers worldwide and iOS users in Australia who will benefit from an open mobile app ecosystem.”

“We will request a stay and appeal the outcome to seek a resolution ​that ​respects our ⁠intellectual property and protects the safe, ​secure experience that consumers ​and ⁠developers expect from the App Store.”

									Apple must open iPhone to alternative app stores in Australia after Epic Games ruling				
				
											
													
						Marcus Mendes | Oct 21 2026 - 8:57 pm PT																
							
																1 Comment							
						
									
			
		
		
			
				
					


	
	

An Australian federal judge has ordered Apple to make sweeping changes to its App Store rules following a years-long antitrust battle with Epic Games. Apple has confirmed that it plans to appeal. Here are the details.

Apple must allow iPhone users with Australian Apple Accounts to install apps from third-party app stores and websites starting March 1, 2027, a federal judge ordered today in a 235-page decision. Apple has until February 15 to request an extension until May 3, 2027, subject to court approval.

Today’s order follows a ruling last year that Apple violated Australian competition law by restricting alternative app distribution and payment methods, in a lawsuit brought by Epic Games similar to its long-running legal battle with Apple in the US.

In his decision, Justice Jonathan Beach said Apple held “a substantial degree of power in the iOS app distribution services market and the iOS in-app payment solutions market,” and used its developer agreements and App Store guidelines to restrict competition.

The ruling also cited Apple’s actions against Epic Games in 2020, including its refusal to allow Epic Direct Pay, Fortnite’s removal from the App Store, and the subsequent termination of Epic’s developer account.

Justice Beach described the latter two actions as “a paradigm example of Apple’s enforcement of its restrictive terms, in contravention of” section 46 of Australia’s Competition and Consumer Act 2010, which prohibits corporations with substantial market power from engaging in conduct that has “the purpose, or has or is likely to have the effect, of substantially lessening competition” in that market.

As a result, Justice Beach issued a wide-ranging series of orders requiring Apple to, among other things:

The decision also addresses several other aspects of Apple’s App Store policies, including restrictions on its ability to turn off apps installed outside the App Store and requirements related to notarization.

The court also prohibited Apple from requiring developers to report transactions processed through alternative payment providers or offer Apple’s payment system alongside their preferred alternatives, both of which are requirements the company imposes in other regions, including Brazil and Japan.

When it comes to Apple’s wins in the decision, the list is much slimmer. Judge Beach rejected Epic’s request to extend the court’s injunctions worldwide and allowed Apple to maintain security scanning and notarization requirements for apps distributed outside the App Store. And while Apple must permit competing app marketplaces on iOS, it is not required to distribute them through its own App Store. This is a distinction he had already established in last year’s ruling.

Finally, the court ordered Apple to pay 85% of Epic’s legal costs incurred through the original trial, while reserving a decision on costs associated with the subsequent hearings over remedies.

Commenting on the decision, Epic confirmed “Fortnite is coming back to the App Store in Australia tomorrow,” and celebrated it as “great news for developers worldwide and iOS users in Australia who will benefit from an open mobile app ecosystem.”

“We will request a stay and appeal the outcome to seek a resolution ​that ​respects our ⁠intellectual property and protects the safe, ​secure experience that consumers ​and ⁠developers expect from the App Store.”

news.article_content:

While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat																				
				
																									
						

	
									
									
										

			Sarah Perez
	

									
									
								
					
					
						12:30 PM PDT · October 21, 2026											
																			
					
		
	





			
					
		
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
	





	
	
		
		
			
Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.

The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely. Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.

Now it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart president and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club.

It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.

What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent.

The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do.

With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.

The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified and you can cap their spending.

The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary.

Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent.

Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site.

news.title: Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
news.title_en: Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
Wednesday’s release of fixes for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP caused administrators and security staff to race to identify and patch vulnerable websites and apps, while attackers inevitably reverse engineered the fixes to learn how to exploit the flaws. Some governments and other groups even proactively took key websites down in anticipation of the release, so they wouldn't be targeted before they could apply the patches.

But in addition to detecting such active exploitation on Wednesday, research published Wednesday evening by Amazon Web Services indicates that at least one actor had started attempting to exploit the bugs—known collectively as PHP2Shell—on October 17, four days before Wednesday's public revelations.

AWS analysts spotted the October 17 exploitation on Wednesday while looking back at activity on one of their so-called honeypots, or intentionally vulnerable web servers or other digital lures that help researchers study attack methods and trends. The attempt came from an IP address that AWS says is linked to a “commercial anonymization network,” in other words a proxy network or VPN.

“While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure,” CJ Moses, AWS's chief information security officer, wrote in the research post.

Proof-of-concept exploits for PHP2Shell began emerging publicly on Wednesday, with some seeming to appear hours before the public disclosure at 10 am ET. In the hours leading up to the disclosure, AWS researchers say their honeypots were hit with multiple exploitation attempts anonymized using various providers and seemingly with various attack goals, likely indicating multiple different actors. “Technical analysis is ongoing, and it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems,” Moses wrote. He added that “PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.”

The PHP Foundation did not immediately respond to WIRED's request for comment.

Though it is unclear how the exploitation on October 17 happened or where it came from, AWS emphasizes that the findings underscore how coordinated vulnerability disclosure must evolve and speed up, given global access to AI tools that can accelerate vulnerability analysis and allow less technically proficient actors to quickly develop new exploits.

“The time from patch to working exploit is shrinking for structural reasons,” Moses wrote. “In the past, most exploitation we observed came after a public proof of concept was released. A small number of capable actors built exploits, and everyone else waited for them. That dependency is weakening. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff or advisory into a working exploit. As a result, more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed.”

news.title: GM says it plans to debut OnStar AI, an in-car assistant that can execute vehicle functions and run diagnostics via voice commands, in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq (Aarian Marshall/Wired)
news.title_en: GM says it plans to debut OnStar AI, an in-car assistant that can execute vehicle functions and run diagnostics via voice commands, in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq (Aarian Marshall/Wired)
news.author: Wired
news.article_content:
But GM does want to make car time better. Or, as Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson put it in an interview with WIRED, “make it more productive, make it more relaxing, make it more engaging. We’d like to make your vehicle a more central, more useful part of your life than it has been historically.” Your future car is sort of a personal assistant, and sort of a spouse, and sort of a tool, and sort of a best friend.

It’s a tall order. But in a raft of announcements this week, GM hopes to demonstrate that, armed with AI-enabled capabilities, the automaker is inching closer to that future.

Courtesy of General MotorsGM also says it will use AI to speed up new-vehicle development, eventually cutting its four- to five-year development time in half—the speed at which Chinese carmakers create new vehicles today.

The automaker plans to expand its “eyes-off” highway driving technology to its most popular cars, inching closer to its years-old promise of making a personal self-driving car. It previously said the system was coming to the Cadillac Escalade IQ in 2028. Today, the company’s Super Cruise feature lets drivers take their hands off their steering wheels on hundreds of thousands of miles of pre-mapped highways. Reaching true autonomy will take time, but GM isn’t ready to talk about that publicly. “This industry is rife with promises that were not fulfilled. I am not keen on making them,” Anderson says.

But GM is taking a different approach from, say, Tesla. The electric carmaker sells a driver-assistance feature called “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” that can navigate many highways and local roads but requires drivers to stay alert and ready to take over at any moment. That kind of system “presents the illusion of autonomy without its benefits,” Anderson says, who for a time led Tesla’s Autopilot program. If drivers can’t do other things while their car is doing most of the driving, it’s less useful and “comes with the direct expense of the safety of your vehicle and the people around you,” he says. “That would not be a responsible way to operate.”

Courtesy of General MotorsGM’s method, by contrast, is to slowly expand “eyes-off” capabilities to more sorts of roads, letting drivers text or eat or watch YouTube first on some highways, and then on more highways, and then on local roads, and then maybe everywhere.

That’s when the automaker's vision gets bigger and blurrier. The cabin, the company says in a blog post, can become a space to “relax, work, and unwind. … In time, this will pave the way for a future where your car can take on everyday errands,” the company says. The personal self-driving car will pick up groceries, drop off children, and then maybe even find a parking spot at the end.

Urban planners and infrastructure experts have worried about this vision. If you lower the price of a car trip, in money and time spent driving, won’t everyone send their cars out for every task? Won’t the roads be crowded with pods full of people sleeping, emailing, and YouTubing while their vehicles slowly pilot them onward—or worse, cars with no one in them? Won’t cities become sprawlier?

Anderson says yes. If you have cheap, personal driving robots, “you will very likely incur more of those robots on the roads. And so there's a lot of societal and infrastructural considerations to make here,” he says. But he argues we have time, and that cities take time to sprawl. “I wouldn't call this an imminent thing, but it certainly is something we should be thinking about.”

news.title: Cloud provider Railway says an unauthorized party may have accessed customer encrypted environment variables and, for some, obtained the decrypted contents (Jacob Cooper/Railway Blog)
news.title_en: Cloud provider Railway says an unauthorized party may have accessed customer encrypted environment variables and, for some, obtained the decrypted contents (Jacob Cooper/Railway Blog)
news.author: Railway Blog
news.article_content:
BlogGo to HomepageJacob CooperOct 21, 2026Security Disclosure: Wednesday October 21stEarlier this morning, Railway detected anomalous activity involving systems that store customer environment variables. After further investigation, our investigation to date indicates that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents. Environment variables may contain secrets such as API keys or database and registry credentials.

We believe this is part of a series of attacks recently targeting platform companies with the aim of compromising AI inference providers. We have notified these upstream providers to revoke all keys proactively, as we take these kinds of events extremely seriously.

While our initial analysis suggests the impact may be limited to a subset of users, we are nevertheless recommending that all users take the actions described below as a precaution to protect your systems while we complete our review.

What you should do: As such, we strongly recommend that you immediately roll all environment variables, including any API keys, stored in Railway, as well as any private registry credentials, and review logs for those services for unusual activity.

All deployments are paused while we investigate. Until builds are restored, you will not be able to roll out new versions. We apologize for this inconvenience. Follow this incident to be notified when builds resume.

As we confirm which accounts were affected, we will contact those customers directly by email with additional details.

We will provide new updates on this announcement, and on status.railway.com as we narrow the scope of impact.

news.title: AuxoAI, which helps large businesses build and deploy AI systems, raised a $20.7M Series A led by NTTVC to accelerate growth and scale (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
news.title_en: AuxoAI, which helps large businesses build and deploy AI systems, raised a $20.7M Series A led by NTTVC to accelerate growth and scale (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
news.author: SiliconANGLE
news.article_content:
SHARE


	
	
		
			
				
					
						UPDATED 09:00 EDT / OCTOBER 20 2026

AuxoAI Inc., an enterprise engineering and consulting company that helps large businesses build and deploy artificial intelligence systems, today announced it has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding to accelerate growth and scale its enterprise AI consulting model.

The company said it has spent over three years working with Global 2000 enterprises and strategic partners, bringing AI into the core of their operations.  It focuses on combining business-process expertise, data engineering and AI agents – autonomous systems that use artificial intelligence to work with little or no human oversight, with deep insight into company data to complete long-term tasks.

AuxoAI builds AI solutions by sending on-site engineers and strategy teams to understand enterprise culture, data, workflow automation and customer engagement to tailor experiences to business and employee needs.

At the core of the company’s platform is Damia, which the company describes as an FDE Workbench, or “forward-deployed engineer” toolkit that also transforms data into applications and licenses for customers. It combines reusable agent capacities with tools for capturing a company’s business knowledge and processes.

The company said that over the years, it has learned how to work with customers to encode relevant knowledge and relationships and use that to create AI agents around the company’s processes. This preserves what the team learns in software and structured knowledge, rather than only interviews or paper documents, but in living software that can work alongside employees.

The company calls this effect “intelligence embedded in the work itself,” where consulting treats AI as a lever or tool for the customer rather than an end product.

AuxoAI partners with companies that businesses already know and trust, including Google LLC, Amazon Web Services Inc., Snowflake Inc., Databricks Inc. and Microsoft Corp., allowing the company to provide enterprise-ready AI, cloud, data and productivity via these platforms.

NTT Venture Capital, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm backed by Japanese technology conglomerate NTT Inc., led the funding round. The round also included participation from prominent industry executives and strategic investors, such as George Still Jr., partner emeritus at Norwest Venture Partners; Amit Zavery, president, chief product officer and chief operating officer at ServiceNow Inc.; and Giacomo Sonnino, managing director at Charlesbank Capital Partners and former chief operating officer of Quantum Black North America.

NTTVC’s portfolio includes Anthropic PBC, which will bring on another major artificial intelligence leader to extend AuxoAI’s capabilities.

The company said the new funding will serve to accelerate the next phase of its journey to expand its global reach. It aims to provide onsite consulting talent for enterprise AI transformation, invest in proprietary technology and AI-native delivery capabilities, and scale up its presence and strategic ecosystem.

news.title: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
news.title_en: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
During a dinner with Meta board members on September 9, Zuckerberg informed them that he was considering leaving California because of the measure, known as Proposition 40, and that he planned to list his Palo Alto, California home for sale four days later, the 109-page filing stated. The ballot proposal, which could be subject to lawsuits even if voters approve it, calls for a one-time 5 percent tax on stock and other assets held by billionaires in the state as of January 2026.

Many wealthy individuals, including Zuckerberg, currently avoid significant tax payments by borrowing against their shares and taking low salaries—$1 annually in the Meta CEO’s case. Zuckerberg purchased a home in Florida this past February, the Wall Street Journal reported at the time.

His potential cross-country move concerned a special committee of the board, whose members included attorney Robert Kimmitt, venture capitalist Charlie Songhurst, and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu. “The special committee was mindful about the difficulties the company faced during the COVID-19 pandemic when Zuckerberg could not be physically present with the company’s management team and did not want the company to face similar challenges going forward,” according to Wednesday’s filing.

Within days of the Meta board dinner, the special committee and Zuckerberg reached an agreement that links his ability to sell special company shares to his continued residence in California. It was finalized a week ago, and on Wednesday, Meta announced the details. It plans to create a new class of shares that hold no voting power. Selling these shares could potentially help raise funds for Meta’s expensive investments into AI data centers, without diluting Zuckerberg’s existing voting control.

All existing shareholders will receive the new nonvoting shares automatically in proportion to their existing holdings. Under what Meta called a “Founder Alignment Agreement” with Zuckerberg, he can sell 20 percent of those new shares to help pay any taxes he may owe. The remaining 80 percent would be available for sale in chunks over the next eight years as long as he remains in California. Any attempt to sell them early would require offloading some of his voting shares “unless there are material unforeseen circumstances that would render it prudent or advisable for Zuckerberg to reside elsewhere.”

Notably, the agreement specifies that Zuckerberg merely has to remain wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, so it’s possible that both he and the company could move together to another state. A number of California companies left for Texas, Nevada, and other states in recent years. Google cofounders Sergey Brin and Larry Page are among the handful of billionaires widely believed to have exited California over the potential tax.

But with much of the most pioneering AI development happening in Silicon Valley, leaving the city of Menlo Park could be a difficult proposition for the Meta board to stomach. “The goal is to keep Zuckerberg continuing to lead the company from California and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs,” the filing stated, referring to the company unit behind its recent Muse AI models.

In the end, the exercise may have been for naught. Recent polling in California suggests that with about $129 million spent campaigning against Prop 40, it will fail to muster enough votes.

news.title: GitLab patches a critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed servers, affecting every release since 7.0 in 2014 (Swati Khandelwal/The Hacker News)
news.title_en: GitLab patches a critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed servers, affecting every release since 7.0 in 2014 (Swati Khandelwal/The Hacker News)
news.author: The Hacker News
news.article_content:
GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014.

The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the October 12 update covered only versions 19.2 and later, and the new fixed versions sit one patch above it, so an instance updated then is in range again.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, is rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale, the maximum. GitLab says that, under certain conditions, it could allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code on the server due to an integer overflow during the compilation of a specially crafted regular expression.

GitLab has not said what those conditions are. The company reports no sign the flaw has been used in attacks, and it is not listed in the U.S. CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of October 22.

Only self-managed installations need to act. GitLab.com already runs the fixed version, and GitLab Dedicated tenants on the internal releases 19.3.5-internal0 and 19.4.2-internal0 or later already have the fix.

The table below pairs each release branch with the version that fixes it.

Four of those versions are older than GitLab normally patches. The company's policy covers the current release and the previous two monthly releases, which, as of today, are 19.5, 19.4, and 19.3.

GitLab said it backported this fix to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, and 19.2.9 on top of its standard releases, a step it reserves for severe issues.

The reason the flaw reaches so far back is the part of GitLab that failed. The regular-expression compiler is Ruby's built-in engine, called Onigmo, which GitLab ships inside its own packages and patches in its own builds. A weakness in that engine is present wherever GitLab has shipped it, which is every release since 7.0.

GitLab also published two detection rules to help self-managed administrators look for exploitation attempts, named "Onigmo native worker crash" and "Org mode render error burst." They are part of the company's open-source TLDR framework, which writes each detection in the Sigma format against GitLab's own application logs.

GitLab has not said what preconditions an attacker needs to reach the compiler, so administrators cannot yet rule themselves out by configuration; the fix is the only certain protection, and GitLab's advisory offers no interim workaround.

This is the fourth code-execution flaw in GitLab's regular-expression engine that the same researcher, who uses the handle joaxcar, has reported in a month, and the first to reach versions before 19.2.

On October 12, GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, also an unauthenticated 10.0 overflow in the regex compiler, in versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. On September 23, it fixed two more, CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-89078, both rated 9.9 but requiring a logged-in account. The three earlier flaws stopped at version 19.2; this one does not.

The October 21 release fixes 11 security issues in all, one critical and the rest high, medium, or low.

Two of the others concern authentication. CVE-2026-15723, rated high at 8.2, could allow a logged-in user to take over another account, but only when an administrator has enabled both SAML and LDAP auto-linking.

A cache-poisoning flaw in GitLab's OAuth and OpenID Connect endpoints, CVE-2026-112212, rated high at 7.5, could allow an attacker to redirect certain sign-in flows to a server they control in setups that use a shared cache.

The upgrade carries a cost worth planning for. The 19.4.3 and 19.3.6 releases include database changes that run during the upgrade, and on a single-node server that means downtime while they finish. GitLab says multi-node setups can apply the patch without downtime using its zero-downtime procedure.

news.title: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
news.title_en: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
Enterprise-sized businesses spend, on average, 28 percent of their software budgets on unwanted upgrades, migrations, and licensing changes. Often, those firms' IT heads think those changes are detrimental.

Those results are according to a survey of 2,018 chief information officers and senior IT decision-makers at companies with at least 10,000 employees that Origina commissioned for its report, “The Software Tax.” About half of the respondents (1,011) are from the US, and the rest are from the United Kingdom. All respondents worked at companies with at least $1 billion in annual revenue.

Keep in mind that Origina provides maintenance for various enterprise software. Its report points to independent software maintenance as a way for IT leaders to regain control over software budgets, illustrating its potential bias. A third-party research consultancy, Censuswide, conducted the survey.

news.title: Mark Zuckerberg says Muse has drawn 10M+ users since its launch and 25%+ of users are making purchases through the app, with an average purchase size of $200+ (Business Insider)
news.title_en: Mark Zuckerberg says Muse has drawn 10M+ users since its launch and 25%+ of users are making purchases through the app, with an average purchase size of $200+ (Business Insider)
news.author: Business Insider
news.article_content:
Meta's new personal AI agent app has drawn more than 10 million users in the US and Canada since its September launch, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Wednesday.

During Meta's third-quarter earnings call, Zuckerberg said that Muse's growth "continues to be strong" and that the most common use case for the agent is shopping.

More than a quarter of Muse users are making purchases through the app, with an average purchase size of over $200, Zuckerberg said.

Beyond shopping, CFO Susan Li said on the call that Muse users most often use it for "personal productivity," connecting their email and calendars to the agent.

Meta's stock had surged after it released Muse. Its stock was up 5% after-hours on Wednesday.

The agent, which Meta says can help users handle tasks like sending an email or booking travel, quickly climbed to the top of Apple's App Store after its release, giving Zuckerberg an early win for his enormous AI spending.

Earlier on Wednesday, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for misleading users about how it handled their data and for failing to prevent misinformation on Facebook.

Move over, Facebook. Zuckerberg seems to have a new favorite product.

Want more Business Insider in your news feed?
                                  
                                    Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.

Add to Preferred Sources
                                  
                                
                              
                                    
                  
                  
                    
                  In Zuckerberg's opening remarks, he mentioned Muse nearly 50 times. Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp were only mentioned once.

"Muse went from an idea on a whiteboard to a successful product in just about eight months, and we're about to ship Muse Charm, which will have gone from concept to a hardware device in people's pockets in less than a year," Zuckerberg said on the call.

"I think that we are going to work on monetization somewhat sooner on this than our normal playbook for a couple of reasons," Zuckerberg said. "One is just the size of the numbers that we are talking about in terms of both the costs and the opportunity… make it important to make progress on that in order to be able to scale it."

The other reason, he said, is "such a large part of what people are doing is commerce."

Li added that Meta sees multiple paths to monetization, beginning with paid subscriptions. "We also see a significant opportunity to extend Muse to small businesses," she said.

Zuckerberg said Muse should remain free for most users, with Meta planning to make money from it through commerce tools that take a fee from transactions it helps facilitate.

He also said Muse is set to arrive on Meta's smart glasses next month, calling Muse "central to the business model for the glasses."

"We expect Muse and having your personal superintelligence with you throughout the day will be the most important part of the experience," he said.

Meanwhile, Forrester principal analyst Kate Winick said Wednesday that the biggest X-factor in Meta's AI ambitions is consumer trust.

"The more information Muse has, the more effective it can be, and overall trust in Meta remains low," Winick said.

She added, "But Meta has cultivated a reputation that negates trust as a condition for engagement: consumers almost expect to have their data mismanaged in exchange for a high level of connectivity and utility, and have shown that they're willing to keep showing up as long as the product experience delivers."

news.summary_en: During the third-quarter earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg announced that Meta's new personal AI agent app Muse has drawn over 10 million users across the US and Canada since its September rollout, rapidly climbing to the top of the Apple App Store. Shopping has emerged as its primary use case, with over 25% of users completing transactions inside the app at an average purchase size exceeding $200. news.title_zh: 扎克伯格称个人智能助手用户破千万且两成用户下单带货
news.summary_zh: 扎克伯格在季度财报会上透露其个人智能体应用用户突破千万，超四分之一用户完成购物且客单价超两百美元
news.article_content_zh:
在三季度财报电话会议中，公司首席执行官向投资者披露，九月推出的个人智能体在北美市场上线后迅速积攒了超过一千万活跃用户。除了协助用户收发邮件和同步日程等日常办公生产力场景外，后台数据显示该应用最普遍、粘性最高的使用场景竟然是电商导购。不仅整体转化率超过百分之二十五，单笔平均订单金额更是突破了两百美元大关。

该产品的快速普及不仅助推其登顶苹果应用商店免费榜，也给近期持续承压的管理层打了一剂强心针。此前，由于在数据处理方式及虚假信息监管方面存在过失，公司刚刚遭遇法庭高额判罚；而这款主打个人助手的消费级应用在商业变现端的超预期表现，迅速提振了二级市场的信心，推动股价在盘后交易阶段逆势上扬。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在最新公布的三季度财报电话会议上，扎克伯格宣布旗下九月新推出的个人智能体应用在北美地区用户量已突破千万大关，并迅速登顶苹果应用商店榜首。数据显示该应用最核心的使用场景为购物，超过四分之一的用户直接在对话中完成下单，平均客单价突破两百美元。这一亮眼表现不仅为该公司此前遭受质疑的庞大技术资本支出提供了首个强力变现证据，也标志着其商业重心正向对话式电商深度转移。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: During the third-quarter earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg announced that Meta's new personal AI agent app Muse has drawn over 10 million users across the US and Canada since its September rollout, rapidly climbing to the top of the Apple App Store. Shopping has emerged as its primary use case, with over 25% of users completing transactions inside the app at an average purchase size exceeding $200. The strong momentum offers early commercial vindication for the company's aggressive AI capital expenditures while pivoting conversational interfaces into direct commerce funnels.

elements_zh.why: 向华尔街证明其巨额算力投入能够转化为高客单价的交易闭环，探索下一代社交电商入口

elements_en.what: Reported that the new personal AI agent reached 10M+ users with over 25% making purchases at a $200+ average basket size
elements_en.why: To demonstrate tangible commercial ROI on aggressive AI infrastructure spend by creating a conversational shopping funnel

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 兜兜转转这么多年，管理层终于想通了：别跟华尔街画通用人工智能的星辰大海，能在聊天框里把货卖出去才是硬道理。上一季还在被分析师追问几百亿芯片怎么回本，这头就把对话机器人硬生生做成了海外版带货窗口，连两百多美元的客单价都吹得有模有样。哪怕白天刚被法院开出天价数据罚单，只要财报里带货数据够诱人，资本市场立刻就能把前嫌忘得一干二净。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Tech giants have finally realized that abstract AGI dreams don't appease Wall Street—turning a chatbot into a high-ticket checkout counter does. After quarters of scrutiny over whether GPU spending would ever pay off, packaging conversational agents as frictionless digital personal shoppers makes the narrative instantly palatable. Even a massive regulatory penalty earlier that day couldn't spoil the post-earnings party once investors saw the lucrative transaction figures.

The strong momentum offers early commercial vindication for the company's aggressive AI capital expenditures while pivoting conversational interfaces into direct commerce funnels.

news.title: Anthropic unveils Claude Duet, a proactive agent app on iOS, Android, and the web that works in the background, in research preview for US Pro and Max users (Claude)
news.title_en: Anthropic unveils Claude Duet, a proactive agent app on iOS, Android, and the web that works in the background, in research preview for US Pro and Max users (Claude)
news.author: Claude
news.article_content:
CategoryAnnouncementsDateOctober 21, 2026Reading time5 minShareCopy linkToday, we’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working even when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. We built Claude Duet for professionals and small business owners with more on their plates than they can track.

We designed Claude Duet to be a partner you can trust. Professionals of all kinds have to juggle many decisions a day, and we think they’ll find Claude Duet most useful. It helps you prioritize where to spend your time and energy, and to leave room for the ambitious projects that felt impossible or daunting before.

Each morning, it sends you a short brief on the most important items across your connected apps. Throughout the day, it keeps tabs on those apps and messages you only when something needs your attention. You can also hand it tasks of all shapes—from simple administrative tasks of scheduling meetings to more complex ones, such as building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps.

Claude Duet draws on years of security, safety, and privacy work on agents, both our own and the infrastructure businesses use to run theirs:

How Duet handles sensitive information. We’re also releasing Claude Duet with a new dedicated classifier and safety system prompt that checks each message and guards against leaks of sensitive information. An agent that reads email and sends messages for you is constantly deciding where information should go. This new classifier and prompt are designed to reject requests to share the strictest tier of information, including credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, such as health or personal finances, are let through only when you’ve explicitly instructed Claude Duet to send it.

We’re continuing to develop and strengthen these protections, and will share more details about how Claude Duet is designed for safety in the coming days.

People at Anthropic have been using Claude Duet to accomplish more, but also to leave more room for thinking and being present. Boris Cherny, who leads our Claude Code team, talks through his mental to-do list with Claude Duet on walks, instead of saving the work for his desk. Chelsea Larsson, who leads our model and product behavior design team, hands Claude Duet her to-do list before leaving to be with her kids and it saves the results for an evening report. And the team behind Claude Duet uses it to build the product. Karan Ahuja, who leads the team, works with it to schedule user interviews, partner with him on prototypes, and even ship code.

We gave small business owners and entrepreneurs early access to Claude Duet, and some have been using it to help run their businesses. Here’s what some of them said:

Jess gets a rundown from Claude Duet each morning. One day, without being asked, it flagged a property showing that was on her calendar for the wrong day. “[This is] exactly the kind of thing I want caught without having to ask,” she said.

Amin owns Shahs of Kabob in South Florida with about 110 employees. He’s used Claude Duet for accounting, customer support, and marketing, and has worked through his invoices store by store. “It brings it all together,” he said. “I don’t need to open up 100 tabs.”

Mya had a call coming up with a potential client. Claude Duet saw it on her calendar and prepared a brief. It also noticed the call fell right before her flight and offered to move it. “I didn’t realize that it was right before my flight,” she said. “I love that proactivity.”

Your context from Claude is the foundation. Claude Duet carries over your memory, skills, and connected apps from your Claude account, so setting it up requires minimal work. What changes is how you work together: Claude Duet comes to you first, and you can message it through typing or voice in one ongoing thread, so a quick reply and a weeklong project both start in the same place.

Work continues when you step away. Claude Duet has a virtual machine with its own browser, so it doesn’t require your laptop or phone to be on. Describe a task in a short message, and it works out which apps to use and what steps to take in the background. You’ll receive a notification when the task is complete or needs your review.

Receive a message when something needs you. Claude Duet checks your connected accounts every few hours, because checking nonstop would use up your plan’s limits much faster. We’re continuing to test its judgment about when to message you, and we’ll keep tuning it based on what testers tell us. You can also tell it what you want to hear about and how often.

Important decisions stay with you. Claude Duet reads, drafts, and prepares work on its own. But before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your approval. A few things are off-limits even with your approval, like trading securities or moving money between accounts. You’re also able to disconnect any app Claude Duet has access to.

This is an early version of Claude Duet, and it still might misread a thread or miscalibrate what’s urgent. We built its core functionality around work, so personal errands, such as booking tickets, aren’t quite as strong, and it can’t yet show you its browser. For now, Claude Duet lives in its own app, separate from the main Claude app. What we learn from early users will shape how the two work together.

During the research preview, Claude Duet shares your plan’s usage limits with the rest of Claude, and it uses them differently than a typical conversation does. Its background checks count toward those limits, and larger tasks, like building a financial model or a deck, require more model turns and background work.

Explore more product news and best practices for teams building with Claude.

news.summary_en: Anthropic has rolled out a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive autonomous agent application spanning iOS, Android, and web platforms for premium subscribers. Moving beyond passive question-and-answer chatbots, the agent runs continuously in the background across connected tools, compiling morning priority briefings and executing multi-step tasks while pinging users only when decisions or permissions are required. The initiative marks a strategic shift toward proactive digital co-workers capable of autonomously coordinating complex administrative workflows.
news.title_zh: 人工智能新星推出主动型后台智能体应用测试版
news.summary_zh: 大模型领军企业推出主动型智能体应用预览版，可在后台静默运行并跨多应用主动提醒与协同执行任务
news.article_content_zh:
该产品被定位于专业人士与中小企业经营者的全天候数字协同伙伴。与常见的对话式机器人不同，新版应用主打主动性和后台持续执行能力。每天清晨，应用会根据用户授权连接的多项工作软件，自动整合出亟待处理的重难点待办清单，并在整个工作日内保持静默追踪，仅在关键节点向用户请求授权或呈报异常。

在任务执行维度，该智能体支持从会议日程统筹等基础行政事务，跨越到复杂的数据仪表盘搭建、销售预测建模乃至基础原型开发。团队在设计中强调了安全边界，任何涉及替用户采取不可逆操作的行为，均必须获得用户的显式确认，以此在自动化效能与操作可控性之间寻找平衡。

ai_analysis.insight_en: Chatbots have finally evolved from reactive assistants into seasoned corporate operators that work quietly in the background and only tap your shoulder when an approval is due. But having an AI constantly surveying all your enterprise software to assign you daily priorities sounds less like liberation and more like an infallible digital micro-manager. Once the machine proactively schedules meetings and builds dashboards for you, blaming administrative chaos for missed deadlines is officially off the table.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 知名大模型创新团队正式上线了一款名为主动副驾的全新智能体应用研究预览版，同步覆盖移动设备与网页端。该应用突破了传统一问一答的交互模式，能够在系统后台持续静默运行，主动抓取所关联工作软件的上下文并向用户推送早报，只有在关键决议或需要核准操作时才会主动发起打扰。此举旨在将大模型从被动应答的虚拟顾问转变为能够主动代办跨平台复杂日程的数字化办公协作者。

Moving beyond passive question-and-answer chatbots, the agent runs continuously in the background across connected tools, compiling morning priority briefings and executing multi-step tasks while pinging users only when decisions or permissions are required. The initiative marks a strategic shift toward proactive digital co-workers capable of autonomously coordinating complex administrative workflows.

news.title: Broad access through consistent standards
news.title_en: Broad access through consistent standards
news.author: OpenAI 官方动态
news.original_content: How OpenAI works with distribution partners to uphold consistent safeguards, support responsible access, and clarify expectations in our Usage Policies.
news.content_snippet: How OpenAI works with distribution partners to uphold consistent safeguards, support responsible access, and clarify expectations in our Usage Policies.
news.summary_en: OpenAI published updated ecosystem guidance outlining consistent security standards and usage policies for its global distribution partners. The framework mandates that downstream distributors and solution providers adhere to identical baseline safety guardrails and responsible access requirements when integrating and reselling foundational models. The move is designed to mitigate escalating regulatory liabilities from widespread distribution while tightening centralized control across its expanding developer ecosystem.

news.summary_zh: 领先技术机构面向全球分销合作伙伴出台统一安全规范，明确合规接入底线与生态治理要求
news.article_content_zh: 该份规范文件重点阐明了源头模型提供方如何与全球分销商协同落地安全防线的细则。随着大模型能力被越来越多地嵌入企业级应用、云服务商平台及第三方行业解决方案，如何防止模型能力在二次开发中被滥用成为了监管层重点关注的焦点。新出台的指引对各类下游接入方在调用频率、敏感领域过滤和最终用户审计等方面提出了更为细致的刚性要求。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 大模型行业领航机构在其最新官方生态指引中，正式明确了与全球分销伙伴的统一安全防线与使用规范。文件要求所有下游渠道商在分发底层技术和提供服务接口时，必须严格贯彻一致的安全防护机制与滥用防御措施，确保技术在多层级转售场景下仍符合既定规则。此举旨在应对伴随渠道扩张而激增的法律与合规风险，同时进一步巩固核心厂商对整个应用生态的绝对主导权。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI published updated ecosystem guidance outlining consistent security standards and usage policies for its global distribution partners. The framework mandates that downstream distributors and solution providers adhere to identical baseline safety guardrails and responsible access requirements when integrating and reselling foundational models. The move is designed to mitigate escalating regulatory liabilities from widespread distribution while tightening centralized control across its expanding developer ecosystem.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 翻译一下就是：想靠分销我的模型吃红利可以，但所有绳套都得按我的尺寸来戴。把加强渠道控制和法律免责切割精心包装成负责任开放的行业担当，既给随时准备找茬的监管部门递上了合规投名状，又顺理成章地给下游所有转售商戴上了金箍。生态繁荣的大旗由它来扛，安全违规的黑锅由分销商去背，这套公关太极打得确实滴水不漏。
ai_analysis.insight_en: In plain terms: you are welcome to make a profit reselling the frontier models, but every leash remains firmly held by the provider. Packaging channel control and liability protection as an altruistic commitment to global safety standards is PR at its finest. It satisfies anxious regulators with ready-made compliance paperwork while ensuring that if an edge case goes haywire, downstream resellers will be the ones taking the blame.

news.title: Filing: Meta says Mark Zuckerberg is considering leaving California if it passes a one-time 5% tax on billionaires; voters will decide on the measure next month (Pierre Paulden/Bloomberg)
news.title_en: Filing: Meta says Mark Zuckerberg is considering leaving California if it passes a one-time 5% tax on billionaires; voters will decide on the measure next month (Pierre Paulden/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.original_content:
Pierre Paulden / Bloomberg:
Filing: Meta says Mark Zuckerberg is considering leaving California if it passes a one-time 5% tax on billionaires; voters will decide on the measure next month  —  Mark Zuckerberg said he is considering leaving California if it passes
news.content_snippet: Mark Zuckerberg said he is considering leaving California if it passes a measure that would impose a one-time, 5% tax on billionaires.
news.summary_en: Mark Zuckerberg disclosed in a regulatory filing that he is considering leaving California if the state passes a proposed one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires in next month's ballot. The measure, which California voters will soon decide on, faces stiff resistance from Silicon Valley leaders seeking to protect their assets. The move underscores growing tensions between tech elites and progressive tax policies in the state.
news.title_zh: 文件：Meta表示，如果加州通过对亿万富翁一次性征收5%的税，马克·扎克伯格将考虑离开加州；选民将在下个月就这项措施作出决定。
news.summary_zh: 更多技术实测与行业影响持续跟踪

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 马克·扎克伯格在监管披露文件中透露，若加利福尼亚州下月投票通过针对亿万富翁征收5%一次性财产税的提案，他正考虑迁出该州。加州选民将在即将到来的公投中对该法案进行表决。扎克伯格此举主要是为了规避潜在的数十亿美元巨额个人税务负担，并向当地立法机构施加政策压力。

news.title: Meta says it will create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital it needs for developing AI models, with an effective date in January 2027 (Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal)
news.title_en: Meta says it will create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital it needs for developing AI models, with an effective date in January 2027 (Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal)
news.author: Wall Street Journal
news.original_content:
Meghan Bobrowsky / Wall Street Journal:
Meta says it will create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital it needs for developing AI models, with an effective date in January 2027  —  The company, which reported record revenue of $64.2 billion for the t
news.content_snippet: The company, which reported record revenue of $64.2 billion for the third quarter, said the new stock won't affect Mark Zuckerberg's voting control
news.summary_en: Meta announced the establishment of a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, scheduled to become effective in January 2027, to finance its aggressive AI model development. The structure enables the company to raise massive public capital for AI infrastructure without diluting Mark Zuckerberg's absolute voting control. The strategic move comes as generative AI training demands unprecedented capital expenditure.
news.title_zh: Meta表示，它将创建一种新的无投票权股票，以筹集开发人工智能模型所需的资金，该股票将于2027年1月生效。

news.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon found critical PHP flaw affecting millions of websites
news.title_en: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon found critical PHP flaw affecting millions of websites
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol discovered a critical PHP vulnerability as part of the Patch the Planet initiative that could affect millions of websites. Security firm Wiz independently found the same flaw using Google's Gemini 4 Argon. OpenAI warns that the same AI capabilities that find vulnerabilities can help attackers too.

The article OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon found critical PHP flaw affecting millions of websites appeared first on The Decoder.

news.summary_zh: 沃尔玛下月起允许第三方AI智能体直接接入代客下单购物，与亚马逊的筑墙封杀策略大相径庭

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 沃尔玛宣布将于下月起正式开放电商接口，允许消费者接入自主选择的第三方AI智能体在其官方网站代为选购并提交订单。平台为此设立了审核把关、预算限额及支付方式锁定等安全护栏，并明令禁止智能体越权操作。这一极度开放的态度与全面封锁竞品AI爬虫与导购助手的亚马逊形成鲜明对立，旨在借助外部AI流量抢占下一代智能零售入口。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Walmart announced plans to permit customers to link personal AI agents directly to its e-commerce platform starting next month, enabling automated shopping within strict spending limits and manual review gates. The retailer laid out clear boundary guidelines to prevent unauthorized payment modifications and out-of-scope actions. The welcoming approach directly counters Amazon's hostile strategy of aggressively banning third-party shopping agents.

elements_zh.where: 全球数字零售与电商平台接口策略发布
elements_zh.what: 下月起全面支持用户自选AI智能体代客在官网下单购物，并设定合规协议规则
elements_zh.why: 与亚马逊的闭门防守形成差异化竞争，争夺智能体时代的电商流量与购物入口

elements_en.where: Global digital retail and web platform deployment
elements_en.what: Allowing customer AI agents to autonomously shop online under defined behavioral constraints
elements_en.why: Countering Amazon's walled-garden approach to capture early autonomous AI commerce traffic

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当亚马逊还在把AI当成盗窃流量的‘网购小偷’严防死守时，沃尔玛已经想通了：管你是人是硅基生物，只要带着钱包来结账就是好顾客。给AI设置花钱限额不仅显得极具前瞻性，还能顺手把‘帮用户管好AI钱包’的护城河给占了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: While Amazon treats incoming shopping bots like digital shoplifters to be banned on sight, Walmart simply asks: does the robot have a valid credit card? Welcoming autonomous shoppers with strict spending collars is both savvy opportunism and a masterclass in hijacking next-gen AI retail traffic.

news.title: Microsoft reveals pricing for Xbox Cloud Gaming without Game Pass, for Xbox Insiders now and others next month: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, 50 for $11.99 (Tom Warren/The Verge)
news.title_en: Microsoft reveals pricing for Xbox Cloud Gaming without Game Pass, for Xbox Insiders now and others next month: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, 50 for $11.99 (Tom Warren/The Verge)
news.author: The Verge

Microsoft is opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming to anyone in November.

Microsoft is opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming to anyone in November.

Tom WarrenCloseTom WarrenSenior CorrespondentPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

ShareGiftIllustration by Alex Castro / The VergeTom WarrenCloseTom WarrenPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Xbox Insiders who don’t have a Game Pass subscription will be able to start purchasing cloud playtime today, ahead of a broader rollout next month. Insiders can access “introductory” launch pricing bundles:

All of these cloud hours will include ad-free cloud gaming, shorter wait times, and higher-quality streaming. These aren’t monthly bundles of hours either, so once you purchased a pack it remains available until the hours are used.

The pay-as-you-go Xbox Cloud Gaming option arrives just in time for Grand Theft Auto VI. I reported earlier this month that Microsoft has secured Grand Theft Auto VI streaming rights, but it’s not yet clear if this will be limited to just Xbox consoles. Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft won’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI to PCs, suggesting that the web browsers and apps that can usually access Xbox Cloud Gaming will not be able to stream Grand Theft Auto VI.

Microsoft also continues to test free, ad-supported cloud gaming for Xbox Insiders, offering up another way to stream games without Game Pass. The free streaming sessions are limited to games you already own, and sessions are capped at one hour.

news.summary_en: Microsoft is officially decoupling Xbox Cloud Gaming from its mandatory Game Pass monthly subscription by launching standalone, pay-as-you-go hourly playtime bundles. Rolling out to Xbox Insiders today and broad consumers next month, packages are priced from $3.99 for 10 hours up to $11.99 for 50 hours with no monthly expiration. The model seeks to lure casual gamers looking for flexibility ahead of massive upcoming blockbuster game releases.
news.title_zh: Microsoft reveals pricing for Xbox Cloud Gaming without Game Pass, for Xbox Insiders now and others next month: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, 50 for $11.99
news.summary_zh: 微软Xbox云游戏面向非订阅会员推出按小时计费模式，低至3.99美元即可享受免广告高画质串流

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软宣布全面打破Xbox云游戏此前必须捆绑Game Pass月度会员订阅的限制，正式推出按时长计费的独立游玩套餐。该方案即日起向内测玩家开放，下月推向所有用户，定价为10小时3.99美元、25小时7.99美元及50小时11.99美元。购买的时长包无过期作废限制，并承诺提供免广告、超低延迟等待和最高流媒体画质，意在降低高门槛、吸引非核心玩家在重磅大作发售周期内灵活消费。

elements_zh.what: 推出无需绑定会员的云游戏独立时长套餐（3.99美元起），时长永久有效不过期
elements_zh.why: 降低云游戏尝试门槛，迎战重磅新游戏周期并拓宽非包月订阅用户的变现渠道

elements_en.where: Official platform feature and pricing announcement
elements_en.what: Introduced non-subscription hourly playtime bundles starting at $3.99 without monthly expiration
elements_en.why: To lower entry friction for casual gamers ahead of major releases and monetize non-subscribers

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 兜兜转转几十年，云游戏终究还是活成了‘赛博网吧’按小时开机充值的模样。虽然按时计费被包装成了永不过期的普惠套餐，但本质上还是因为发现每个月固定交月费的冤大头不够用了，赶紧把只想体验几把大作的散客也网罗进来吸干零钱。
ai_analysis.insight_en: After decades of hyping the post-console streaming revolution, cloud gaming has essentially reinvented the 90s cybercafe hourly punch card. When you realize you've tapped out monthly recurring subscribers, pitching 'pay-as-you-go packs' is the classic pivot to extract loose pocket change from casual tourists.

news.title: Flapping Airplanes, which is working on methods to train AI models using less data and compute and make the chips more efficient, raised $1B at a $6B valuation (Rachel Metz/Bloomberg)
news.title_en: Flapping Airplanes, which is working on methods to train AI models using less data and compute and make the chips more efficient, raised $1B at a $6B valuation (Rachel Metz/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.original_content:
Rachel Metz / Bloomberg:
Flapping Airplanes, which is working on methods to train AI models using less data and compute and make the chips more efficient, raised $1B at a $6B valuation  —  Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised
news.content_snippet: Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised $1 billion in funding at a $6 billion valuation …
news.summary_en: One-year-old AI startup Flapping Airplanes has secured $1 billion in fresh capital, catapulting its valuation to $6 billion. The company develops algorithmic and architectural innovations that slash training data requirements, reduce compute bottlenecks, and optimize chip efficiency. The colossal funding highlights urgent investor appetite for alternatives to brutal brute-force GPU scaling amidst skyrocketing infrastructure bills.
news.title_zh: Flapping Airplanes, which is working on methods to train AI models using less data and compute and make the chips more efficient, raised $1B at a $6B valuation
news.summary_zh: 主打低算力少数据训练AI的初创公司成立仅一年即斩获10亿美元融资，估值飙升至60亿美元

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 成立仅一年的低算力算法与芯片优化初创公司Flapping Airplanes宣布完成10亿美元的新一轮巨额融资，公司投后估值一举冲上60亿美元。该企业致力于打破盲目堆砌海量数据与万卡集群的暴力训练范式，专注研发能以极少数据和算力训练高能效大模型的新型软硬件协同技术。其在资本市场引发的抢投潮，折射出顶级风投在昂贵的算力重负之下，正极力寻找能降本增效的颠覆性底层技术。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: One-year-old AI startup Flapping Airplanes has secured $1 billion in fresh capital, catapulting its valuation to $6 billion. The company develops algorithmic and architectural innovations that slash training data requirements, reduce compute bottlenecks, and optimize chip efficiency. The colossal funding highlights urgent investor appetite for alternatives to brutal brute-force GPU scaling amidst skyrocketing infrastructure bills.

elements_en.where: Silicon Valley venture capital financing round
elements_en.what: Raised $1B at a $6B post-money valuation to develop low-data, compute-efficient training methods
elements_en.why: Investors desperately seek alternatives to unsustainable capital expenditure and GPU scaling bottlenecks

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 成立一年、名字取得像开玩笑一样‘扑翼飞机’的公司，一转眼就能值60亿美元，这就是当下AI淘金热的魔幻底色。当大家都被英伟达的芯片账单逼得快揭不开锅时，只要你宣称能用更少的显卡办成一样的事，风投就会排着队把装满数十亿美金的卡车开进你的后院。
ai_analysis.insight_en: A one-year-old startup cheekily named 'Flapping Airplanes' pulling off a $6 billion valuation perfectly captures the modern AI fever dream. When everyone is bleeding billions paying the Nvidia GPU tax, the mere promise of making AI training cheaper will have venture capitalists racing to dump dump-trucks of cash at your doorstep.
