prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；

prompts.code_snippet:
# Multi-Agent Orchestration Topology
workflow:
  name: Autonomous_Research_And_Delivery_Pipeline
  max_iterations: 3
  nodes:
    - id: planner
      role: Strategic Planner
      prompt: "Decompose user request into discrete verifiable sub-tasks. Output pure JSON DAG."
      next: executor
      
    - id: executor
      role: Tool Specialist
      tools: ["web_search", "read_url", "code_interpreter"]
      prompt: "Execute current sub-task using provided tools. Capture raw evidence."
      next: reviewer
      
    - id: reviewer
      role: Adversarial Critic
      prompt: "Verify executor results against factuality and accuracy requirements. Output PASS or REJECT with specific critique."
      conditional_edges:
        PASS: finish
        REJECT: planner

prompts.temp_advice: 温度 0.4
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

1. What are the immutable fundamental laws of science (e.g. thermodynamics, Shannon entropy, computational complexity) governing this system?

3. Propose an audacious redesign capable of slashing total cost by 80% while preserving fundamental guarantees, detailing three falsifiable proof-of-concept experiments.

","datePublished":"2026-10-22T00:00:00.000Z","dateModified":"2026-10-22T17:48:51.000Z","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Anthropic","url":"https://www.anthropic.com"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Anthropic","url":"https://www.anthropic.com"},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-agent-skills-to-the-agentic-ai-foundation","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-agent-skills-to-the-agentic-ai-foundation"}Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI FoundationPublished

Today, we’re donating Agent Skills, the open standard that gives AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, have integrated Agent Skills since we published the standard in December 2025.

A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file that teaches an agent a specific task or domain, along with any scripts or reference material it needs. We developed skills while working on Claude Code. It handled general knowledge work well, but often lacked the procedural knowledge that real business tasks need. Within weeks of our October 2025 launch, developers published thousands of skills on GitHub and wrote loaders for Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode. We then published Agent Skills as an open standard, under its own GitHub organization and domain, so any agent could use it. So far, 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed.

We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral. Today, we are donating the standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, which we co-founded with Block and OpenAI last year, and to which we donated the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The AAIF will provide a neutral home to the standard going forward, ensuring the community has a say in where Agent Skills go next.

We are donating the Agent Skills name and logo, the GitHub organization, and the agentskills.io domain. You can continue to use the standard or contribute to it without joining the AAIF.

Engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and other companies will maintain the standard as individuals, with David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag as Lead Maintainers.

We’ve proposed starting with a roadmap covering versioned releases, a formal proposal process, and security guidance for people who write and install skills. As with MCP, the project will continue to prioritize community input and transparent decision-making. You can join the project’s Discord to give feedback on proposed specification changes.

Thank you to the developers who built with Agent Skills from the start, and to the teams who brought skills into their products. Read the specification at agentskills.io and join the discussion on GitHub.

items.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
items.title_en: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge - but legal experts say these changes aren't enough to address their concerns. ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 针对科技巨头Meta最新更新的商业条款，多位法学专家公开指出其公关修辞背后的法律漏洞。尽管Meta删除了明示可利用新闻内容训练AI的敏感字眼，但条款中依然保留了允许抓取与客户‘产品或服务相关’全部信息的宽泛表述。这意味着出版商只要在Meta平台投放业务，其整站新闻内容仍可能在未经单独授权的情况下沦为AI训练语料。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Legal scholars revealed that Meta's subtle update to its business terms is mere lip service, leaving loopholes that still permit the company to scrape news sites for AI training. While Meta removed explicit wording on training AI on publishers' content, retained clauses regarding data 'associated with your products or services' effectively grant blanket scraping rights without compensating publishers.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Big Tech's legal phrasing is pure sleight of hand: they removed the phrase 'we will scrape your content' and replaced it with 'everything related to your presence is ours anyway.' As long as publishers don't read the fine print, Meta's AI appetite remains completely uninhibited.

items.summary_en: Meta has re-enabled the sharing feature for its Muse AI tool after addressing a critical security flaw. Independent security researchers previously revealed that Muse shared conversation URLs based on prompt titles directly in public DNS, exposing private user data including company revenue reviews and loan applications. Meta temporarily suspended the feature before deploying technical fixes to secure public links.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Meta宣布重新上线旗下AI工具Muse的链接分享功能。此前安全研究人员爆出严重安全隐患：Muse将用户共享对话的标题直接作为二级域名并写入公开DNS记录，导致包括企业营收复盘报告和贷款申请等高度机密的内容被轻易遍历检索。在紧急叫停并实施底层架构修复后，Meta高管确认相关隐患已排除。

items.title: Sources: OpenAI nears an up to $30B round led by investors from the UAE and Coatue at a $1.25T pre-money valuation, as an "opportunistic" bridge ahead of an IPO (Kate Rooney/CNBC)
items.title_en: Sources: OpenAI nears an up to $30B round led by investors from the UAE and Coatue at a $1.25T pre-money valuation, as an "opportunistic" bridge ahead of an IPO (Kate Rooney/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
OpenAI is closing in on a funding round that could value the artificial intelligence giant at more than $1 trillion ahead of a potential initial public offering.

The San Francisco-based AI company is raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, according to people familiar with the deal, who asked not to be named because the details were confidential. That valuation does not include new capital raised.

Investors from the United Arab Emirates are leading the round alongside Coatue, according to the people. The financing is being positioned as an "opportunistic" bridge ahead of a potential IPO.

OpenAI kickstarted discussions for a new funding round after investors approached the company with proposals in September, as CNBC previously reported. OpenAI told investors on Thursday that it is aiming to secure signatures by the end of next week, but the final size of the round is still being determined, the people said.

Alongside the new investment, OpenAI is negotiating a commercial deal that would secure more computing capacity from the UAE, according to one person. OpenAI told investors in February that it's targeting roughly $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030.

The company confidentially filed its prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, but it has not disclosed exactly when it plans to debut.

OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told employees in August that the AI lab "will be a public company in 2027." The following month, CEO Sam Altman said that "right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public."

Anthropic, OpenAI's chief rival, is also gearing up for what is widely expected to be a massive IPO. The company confidentially filed its prospectus with regulators in June and is actively engaging in meetings with prospective investors, as CNBC previously reported.

The company is reportedly seeking a valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion in its offering. In May, Anthropic closed a $65 billion funding round at a $965 billion valuation.

items.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
items.title_en: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
eMudra, the certificate authority that issued eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server—one had a private encryption key of just 4—said it’s getting out of the business.

V. Srinivasan, chairman of India-based eMudhra Limited, cited increasing costs and complexities of compliance requirements—paired with the business generating just 1 percent of its revenue. He also said that the emergence of organizations providing TLS certificates free of charge further reduced returns on investment when compared to other products and services the company offers.

“However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” the company continued in a Thursday post. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.”

items.summary_en: Embattled certificate authority eMudhra has announced its complete withdrawal from the global SSL/TLS market after a catastrophic security failure. The agency previously issued intermediate TLS credentials so fatally misconfigured that one private key was literally set to the single digit '4', allowing malicious actors to forge spoofed certificates. Facing intense industry backlash and irrecoverable reputational damage, the company cited regulatory burdens and marginal revenue as its rationale for shutting down the unit.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 知名证书颁发机构eMudhra在深陷严重安全丑闻后正式宣布永久退出全球SSL/TLS业务。此前该机构被曝光签发了极其脆弱的中间证书，其中一个私有加密密钥数值竟然直接设为了数字‘4’，使得任何人都能伪造任何网站或邮件服务的合法凭证。面对来自行业内外的口诛笔伐与信誉破产，该机构董事会以合规成本过高且业务营收占比极低为由彻底关闭该条线。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Embattled certificate authority eMudhra has announced its complete withdrawal from the global SSL/TLS market after a catastrophic security failure. The agency previously issued intermediate TLS credentials so fatally misconfigured that one private key was literally set to the single digit '4', allowing malicious actors to forge spoofed certificates. Facing intense industry backlash and irrecoverable reputational damage, the company cited regulatory burdens and marginal revenue as its rationale for shutting down the unit.

elements_zh.who: 数字认证服务商eMudhra及其董事会
elements_zh.where: 全球公钥基础设施（PKI）与网络安全信任链体系
elements_zh.what: 因私钥低至荒谬的数字‘4’遭曝光后，宣布永久关停全球TLS证书业务
elements_zh.why: 致命安全失误导致声誉归零，加之合规成本与免费证书机构竞争导致其利润微薄

elements_en.where: Global PKI and internet security infrastructure
elements_en.what: Shutting down global SSL/TLS operations after issuing credentials with a private key of '4'
elements_en.why: Fatal security negligence shattered industry trust, while surging compliance costs rendered the 1% revenue business unviable

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 用‘4’做私钥，相当于银行金库的大门直接挂了一根挂面当门闩。东窗事发后还抱怨‘舆论发酵不符业务比重’，这就好比肇事司机撞穿承重墙后委屈地说‘我这趟车本来就没赚多少油钱’。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Setting a private encryption key to literally the number 4 is the cryptographic equivalent of securing Fort Knox with a wet noodle. Blaming 'social media amplification' on the way out is pure comedy—as if public outrage is the problem, rather than the fact that your root of trust was built out of cardboard.

任何攻击者此前均可借此轻易伪造任意网站的数字信任凭证

Company board voted to permanently abandon SSL/TLS business amidst heavy backlash

items.title: The Social Society Helping Women Join the AI Boom
items.title_en: The Social Society Helping Women Join the AI Boom
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
Berger and Willdorf having a refreshingly practical take on AI. “This is the most formative technology of our generation, and it’s here,” Willdorf says. “If you choose to sit it out, you are doing yourself a disservice.”

They also practice what they preach, especially as they juggle kids entering college, their own aging parents, and their increasingly in-demand business. “The midlife cognitive and emotional labor is so heavy and so intense that we need an assistant,” Berger says. “Actually, we need the National Guard, but AI will help in the interim.”

Shoshana Berger: Nina and I are both recovering magazine editors. We ended up at a friend's birthday party, and we were both obsessing over Claude, our new French lover. All the other women had glazed eyes while we were talking; they just weren’t part of the conversation. At some point I said, “Nina, I think this might be a business, because all these women need to be doing what we're doing.”

Nina Willdorf: We were super nervous before the first event …

Berger: We needed to take beta blockers and ashwagandha because we were like, wait, we're inviting all of these baller women, these really smart, incredibly accomplished women, and we’re not AI experts. But we have been doing what we usually did as reporters, which is test the tools in a way many women did not seem to be doing.

There's a million reasons for women to bow out of the conversation, and we were like, “no, no, no, you cannot bow out of this conversation if you are going to be relevant in the work world. You need to be fluent.”

Willdorf: We are not like pom-pom advocates for everything about this, but we feel committed to this idea that being involved is really important.

How do you set up expectations around the event for attendees?

Berger: There are rules of engagement for every party. One is we have an ideological parking lot. So if you want to talk about how AI is going to ruin everything, this is not the best space to do that. There are lots of ways in which we are also terrified about AI and find it can be quite menacing, especially for creatives like us, but that's not what we're here to do. We're here to gain fluency, test things out, and reduce our administrative load.

Willdorf: And eat some really good cheese and drink some wine.

Berger: We have everyone bring a laptop and a midlife problem. We call it a midlife quandary. We spend 15 minutes doing what we call library time. We all bring our laptops out, and you work on your problem. And Nina and I kind of walk around the room sherpa-ing people through the experience: “You might want to try this tool, try this LLM instead. Your prompt is feeling a little weak. You're not getting the answer that you like. Let's work on that and iterate.”

Willdorf: Sometimes people are like, “You know what? I don't really want AI to write for me.” And we're like, “Oh no, no, we don't either. Let us show you a couple other things you can think about.”

You’ve had a wait list for these parties since you started. How do you decide who gets to attend?

Willdorf: We have really found that the optimal number is between like eight and 12. When it gets bigger than that, it's a little bit chaotic. Our best events have been ones where there is a magical mix, and you have somebody that works in nonprofit next to somebody who works in design next to somebody who is home with the kids next to a CEO next to someone who works in philanthropy.

Most people, in my experience, cannot immediately identify a software-shaped problem in their life. How do you help people see an issue that AI could actually help with?

Berger: So much of what we're trying to do is show the pragmatic ways in which it's helping with midlife overload. We're often labeled the sandwich generation. We hate that term because it just sounds like we're the tasteless tomato in between two slabs of bread. But the real part of that is that we are dealing with parents who increasingly need help and kids who maybe are launching, maybe not.

One woman came to an event with a mother who was dealing with an Alzheimer's diagnosis, and she wanted to know whether her mother was qualified for long-term care because she had an insurance plan. Well, the insurance carrier sent her a 300-page packet. Who is going to read through that? This is how insurance companies keep you from using your insurance policy. So of course, she fed it to AI. And the AI came back saying, yes, your mother is absolutely qualified for care, and would you like me to write a letter to the insurance company to argue your case?

When I first started out as a consultant, I, in a typical female way, completely lowballed my consulting fee. I fed my proposal to Claude and said, “What's wrong with this? Make this bulletproof.” And it came back and said, “You're not charging enough for this scope of work.” And I was like, “Well, what should I charge?” And it said, “Start by doubling your rate.” I took a deep breath, and I did it. The client did not blink.

I feel that a lot of people don’t want to get near AI because they see slop and get the ick. But you’re talking about something different—using AI for economically valuable tasks.

Berger: The economic value piece is really important, because women have long suffered from being stuck at home as domestic laborers, because we weren't seen as economically valuable in the marketplace, right? So the idea behind Aged Intelligence Society is that if anyone needs to optimize their time, it's women.

In some ways, AI is the new washing machine or the new laundry or whatever it is. It's giving women many, many hours of the day back by offering them automation.

The reason we narrowed the aperture to people 40-plus is that we feel like the product-market fit for women who are over 40 is so spot on. One, because we have very discerning taste after many decades of honing it. We know how to ask really sharp questions. We have very strong bullshit meters, so we're not going to take just the first answer. We're going to keep probing and pushing.

And so we feel like in some ways this tool was built for people who have a certain level of intelligence and accrued experience. It's not really built for young people. It's not built for people who have not already gone through the failure and the friction of life and learned for themselves what makes for a good question.

items.summary_en: Former magazine editors Shoshana Berger and Nina Willdorf have founded a dedicated community aimed at empowering mid-career women to adopt AI tools. Highlighting the crushing cognitive and emotional burdens juggling careers, teenage kids, and aging parents, the founders argue that women cannot afford to sit out the AI boom. The initiative offers hands-on guidance to transform advanced chatbots into indispensable cognitive co-pilots.

items.title: Canva launches Craft, its first image generation model, trained on human-designed templates, available to all users, with plans to support third-party chatbots (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Canva launches Craft, its first image generation model, trained on human-designed templates, available to all users, with plans to support third-party chatbots (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Canva releases its first image generation model																				
				
																									
						

	
									
									
										

			Ivan Mehta
	

									
									
								
					
					
						12:00 PM PDT · October 22, 2026											
																			
					
		
	





			
					
		
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
	





	
	
		
		
			
Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta.

The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms.

Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image.

The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.

That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer. Last year, the platform released its own model that understands designs and layers.

Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab. The model will also be available through the Canva API. Plus, the company plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva’s MCP.

Canva has used a bunch of image models for generation in its platform, so it’s likely that the new models will help save API costs for the company. It said that besides costs, the new model also allows the platform to have better quality and speed control.

In 2024, Canva acquired media generation platform Leonardo.ai. It said that the researchers from Leonardo contributed to the new image model.

Canva said that it is developing two cost-efficient versions of the model, called Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, which will be released soon.

The company was on track for $4 billion in revenue last year. However, it cut its growth forecast for 2026, causing its valuation to reportedly plummet from $42 billion to $35 billion, according to external analysts.

Canva releases its first image generation model																				
				
																									
						

	
									
									
										

			Ivan Mehta
	

									
									
								
					
					
						12:00 PM PDT · October 22, 2026											
																			
					
		
	





			
					
		
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
	





	
	
		
		
			
Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta.

The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms.

Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image.

The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.

That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer. Last year, the platform released its own model that understands designs and layers.

Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab. The model will also be available through the Canva API. Plus, the company plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva’s MCP.

Canva has used a bunch of image models for generation in its platform, so it’s likely that the new models will help save API costs for the company. It said that besides costs, the new model also allows the platform to have better quality and speed control.

In 2024, Canva acquired media generation platform Leonardo.ai. It said that the researchers from Leonardo contributed to the new image model.

Canva said that it is developing two cost-efficient versions of the model, called Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, which will be released soon.

The company was on track for $4 billion in revenue last year. However, it cut its growth forecast for 2026, causing its valuation to reportedly plummet from $42 billion to $35 billion, according to external analysts.

items.title: Sure, let’s smoosh SpaceX and Tesla together, who cares
items.title_en: Sure, let’s smoosh SpaceX and Tesla together, who cares
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Oh sure, SpaceX's credit risk is pretty high because it's about to borrow another $40 billion to spend on Nvidia chips, but who cares about that? SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss a merger!

The degree to which you find this merger compelling likely has to do with the degree to which you believe Elon Musk about wanting to go to Mars, or "spread the light of consciousness," as he put it in this week's SpaceX earnings call (and earlier S-1). Now, a reasonably informed person knows that we don't have the technology - or, frankly, even the raw information to build the technology - in order to support human life in space. …

items.summary_en: Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to formally evaluate a blockbuster corporate merger. The potential union comes as SpaceX faces escalating credit risks while preparing to borrow up to $40 billion for Nvidia computing chips to power AI ambitions. Critics highlight that tying publicly traded Tesla to the cash-burning aerospace venture looks less like interplanetary exploration and more like a high-stakes financial engineering bailout.

items.title: Microsoft and Alphabet join 14 other companies objecting to a plan by OKXICE, a venture of OKX and ICE, to trade blockchain-based versions of their shares (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
items.title_en: Microsoft and Alphabet join 14 other companies objecting to a plan by OKXICE, a venture of OKX and ICE, to trade blockchain-based versions of their shares (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
items.author: Fortune
items.article_content:
The two tech giants joined Goldman Sachs, Caterpillar, McDonald’s, Qualcomm, and Western Digital in a new batch of objections disclosed Monday. They joined nine companies—Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group—whose objections were disclosed last week.

Cuomo downplayed the wave of objections, framing the pushback as a predictable reaction to a major market shift.

“We always anticipated that—because this is such a dramatic and revolutionary change—many companies would want to wait and see how it goes rather than be the first to participate,” he said in a written statement to Fortune.

OKX did not respond to questions about when trading would begin or whether the objections had changed its launch plans.

The objections come two weeks after Cuomo announced plans to launch OKXICE’s tokenized stock-trading platform. The venture, a partnership between crypto exchange OKX and ICE, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, would offer round-the-clock trading in blockchain-based versions of 63 U.S.-listed stocks.

The venture is seeking to use a temporary exemption granted by the Securities and Exchange Commission last month that allows qualifying platforms to offer trading in tokenized stocks without registering as national securities exchanges, provided they meet certain conditions.

Under these rules, trading platforms do not need a company’s permission to offer tokenized versions of its shares. Instead, they must notify the company, which then has 30 days from receiving the notice to object before the platform can proceed.

“There’s not a proactive consent right. Rather, it is a reactive right to object,” said Erin Martin, a partner and co-lead of fintech and digital assets at law firm Morgan Lewis, who spent over a decade as a senior lawyer at the SEC. “If they don’t object within that 30-day notice period, the [venue] can go ahead and start to tokenize and list those securities.”

Applied Optoelectronics, a technology company that makes equipment for high-speed networks, said it objected because the framework is new and its potential effects on the pricing, liquidity, and volatility of its stock remain uncertain.

“At this stage, we don’t see a clear benefit to AOI or our shareholders that justifies these uncertainties,” a spokesperson told Fortune. The company also said investors could mistakenly believe it backed the offering, which it neither sponsored nor endorsed.

The other 15 companies declined to comment or did not respond to requests for comment.

But a company’s objection only blocks trading on that platform under the SEC exemption. It does not stop other firms from offering tokenized versions of its shares overseas or through other legal arrangements.

The 30-day deadline can also create practical problems. Under the SEC’s rules, platforms must send notices to a company’s main executive office, where they could get buried in other mail before reaching its legal team, Martin noted. An unanswered notice lets the platform proceed after the deadline. “It has not been contemplated in the existing SEC order,” Martin said regarding whether a company can pull its stock after the 30-day window closes.

OKXICE’s push to tokenize stocks aims to tap into a $35 billion market, offering investors round-the-clock trading without some of the delays associated with traditional stock markets.

“The market never sleeps, so why should trading? Ownership shouldn’t have office hours,” Cuomo said when he first announced the venture.

But the benefits are less clear for the companies whose shares would be traded.

One concern is that the digital tokens could trade at different prices from the shares they represent on the NYSE or Nasdaq, especially when few people are buying and selling.

Martin, the digital assets specialist at Morgan Lewis, notes that companies have an additional concern when it comes to 24/7 trading. Namely, she points out, they would lose the pause they normally have to announce earnings or other important news while markets are closed, which allows investors time to digest the implications.

Protecting investors also presents hurdles if the software handling trades fails or the firms holding the underlying shares run into trouble, according to risk disclosures detailed in OKXICE’s public notice with the SEC.

Meanwhile, Apple, Nvidia, and Amazon are among the remaining 47 companies that have not yet publicly objected to plans to trade tokenized versions of their shares on OKXICE. As of Wednesday, those that received notices in early October could have until early November to respond, depending on when they received them.

If all 60-plus companies in OKXICE’s planned lineup object within the 30-day window, the platform would have no stocks left from that list to offer under the exemption. Ignoring those objections would mean losing the exemption, Martin said.

If all 60-plus companies in OKXICE’s planned lineup object within the 30-day window, the platform would have no stocks left from that list to offer under the exemption. Ignoring those objections would mean losing the exemption, Martin said.

The two tech giants joined Goldman Sachs, Caterpillar, McDonald’s, Qualcomm, and Western Digital in a new batch of objections disclosed Monday. They joined nine companies—Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group—whose objections were disclosed last week.

Cuomo downplayed the wave of objections, framing the pushback as a predictable reaction to a major market shift.

items.title: The Foundations of Scalable AI
items.title_en: The Foundations of Scalable AI
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
A scalable AI system requires a strong foundation. Data, engineering, platforms, operating models, and governance must converge to work as one. This session from MIT Technology Review’s EmTech Future conference explores what it takes to build that foundation in a highly regulated environment and how a responsible, trustworthy implementation can turn emerging capabilities, including agentic systems, into lasting value for investors.

Jing Wang leads Vanguard’s Center for AI & Insights (CAI), advancing the firm’s AI, machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science capabilities. Her team drives enterprise-wide innovation, research, and delivery, enabling Vanguard to translate emerging technologies into trusted solutions that enhance client experiences, improve investor outcomes, and create measurable business value.

Before her current position, Jing served in a range of leadership roles across Vanguard’s Financial Services, Workplace Solutions, International, and Corporate Services divisions. Throughout her tenure, she has led teams and enterprise initiatives that advanced strategic priorities, strengthened client outcomes, and drove business performance across the firm.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 摩根士丹利、摩根大通等多家美国大型银行近期采取行动，封锁了擅自代表客户登录账户的AI智能体。由于部分用户未授权AI代理获取凭据，银行出于安全合规考虑，正全面限制甚至禁止此类智能体的访问权限，并计划强制将其限制在只读模式内。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Major US banks, including Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, have begun blocking AI agents that log in with customer credentials. Due to unauthorized access and security risks, banks are tightening policies, aiming to restrict these agents to read-only access or blocking them entirely.

elements_zh.who: 摩根士丹利、摩根大通等美国银行
elements_zh.where: 银行网银/API访问场景
elements_zh.what: 封锁AI智能体通过客户凭证进行自动化登录的行为
elements_zh.why: 担忧AI代理带来的安全合规隐患及未经授权的账户操纵

elements_en.who: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and other US banks
elements_en.what: Blocking AI agents from logging in with customer credentials
elements_en.why: Security risks and concerns over unauthorized account actions

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当AI智能体兴奋地帮用户把银行存款挪来挪去时，银行风控系统直接拔了网线。AI想在金融界当管家，得先问问银行愿不愿意让这些‘黑箱代理’动动存款，毕竟银行赚的是手续费，不是AI的‘自动化便捷’。
ai_analysis.insight_en: When AI agents excitedly start shuffling customer funds, the banks simply pull the plug. AI wants to be the ultimate financial butler, but it needs to clear the 'black-box' hurdle first—banks care about risk control, not just the thrill of the automated bottom line.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 摩根士丹利、摩根大通等多家美国大型银行近期采取行动，封锁了擅自代表客户登录账户的AI智能体。由于部分用户未授权AI代理获取凭据，银行出于安全合规考虑，正全面限制甚至禁止此类智能体的访问权限，并计划强制将其限制在只读模式内。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Major US banks, including Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, have begun blocking AI agents that log in with customer credentials. Due to unauthorized access and security risks, banks are tightening policies, aiming to restrict these agents to read-only access or blocking them entirely.
key_points_zh: 多家大行限制AI代理自动登录
主要针对获取用户凭据的操作
未来可能仅开放只读权限
key_points_en: Major banks blocking AI agents
Focus on unauthorized credential usage
Moving towards read-only limitations

Unlike narrated audiobooks from Audible and other providers, the audiobooks created with Virtual Voice in Kindle+ will instead be narrated by AI.

Read full bio
					
	
	


			

	
	
	
		
		
					October 22, 2026, 11:55 am ET

Amazon just rebranded its Kindle Unlimited subscription to become Kindle+, and will continue to offer unlimited reading from an eligible Kindle catalog for $12 a month. It will also expand its audiobook category to include more titles, including some read by AI narrators.

Kindle+ remains a separate subscription from Prime, and users will still be able to borrow up to 20 titles at once.

The upgrade expands the already available audiobook category through the subscription. It’ll also give authors the option to include more eligible audiobooks in Kindle+, including AI-narrated titles.

Amazon hopes to enhance the reading experience by letting users continue their ebooks with virtual narration as they go about their day after putting down their Kindle. Users will now be able to choose from many more available audiobooks, from traditional narrators to those created with Virtual Voice.

Amazon is offering the Virtual Voice service free to authors in the Kindle Direct Publishing (KDP) program. With Virtual Voice, authors can have their books narrated by AI at no cost, potentially reaching a wider audience.

Also: Got an old Kindle? How to resurrect your e-reader with new books

The Amazon KDP program lets authors self-publish their ebooks on Kindle and enroll in Kindle+ (formerly Kindle Unlimited) to reach more readers. Kindle+-enrolled authors earn money for pages read, not per download. The author’s earnings through Kindle+ depend on the month’s payout rate and the total number of pages read.

As a loyal reader and audiobook listener, I could argue that an AI-narrated book detracts from the human dimension of audiobooks. The service could take jobs away from professional narrators, many of whom have followings of their own.

While the audiobook experience differs when created by a narrator versus read by AI, authors enrolled in the KDP program may choose to bypass a human narrator for their audiobooks when a virtual narrator is already available for free.

However, listening to books has been possible on Kindle devices and the Kindle app for years. Some Kindle Unlimited ebooks already included free access to a professionally narrated audiobook, though not all.

Kindle accessibility features like Assistive Reader and VoiceView also enabled listening to text read aloud.

There are very few changes to the Kindle+ subscription. Amazon will not increase the price of Kindle+, and users will still be able to borrow books from Kindle+ as they do now with Kindle Unlimited.

Kindle+ is a rebrand, not a new subscription. Readers will get expanded listening options, but the reading experience remains largely unchanged.

Readers looking for human-narrated and dramatized audiobooks should still use Audible and other platforms, like Libby through their local library, to access them.

items.summary_en: Amazon has rebranded its Kindle Unlimited subscription service as Kindle+ and significantly expanded its audiobook catalog, notably integrating titles narrated by generative AI. The move is aimed at driving down the steep production costs of human narration and rapidly converting long-tail backlists into audio format to better retain subscriber attention.
items.title_zh: 亚马逊将其Kindle Unlimited订阅更名为Kindle+，并扩大了有声读物的访问范围，包括由人工智能（AI）解说的书籍。
items.summary_zh: 亚马逊将电子书包月服务更名为Kindle+，同步扩充有声书资源并大规模引入AI生成旁白配音

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 亚马逊近日对其长期运营的电子书包月服务进行了品牌重塑，正式更名为Kindle+。除常规电子书借阅权益外，新服务重点扩大了有声读物库的覆盖范围，并全面引入由人工智能合成旁白的有声书内容。此举旨在降低专业真人配音的高昂录制成本，利用大模型音频生成技术加速盘活海量中长尾书目，从而抗衡流媒体平台对用户注意力的争夺。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Amazon has rebranded its Kindle Unlimited subscription service as Kindle+ and significantly expanded its audiobook catalog, notably integrating titles narrated by generative AI. The move is aimed at driving down the steep production costs of human narration and rapidly converting long-tail backlists into audio format to better retain subscriber attention.

elements_zh.where: Kindle+ 全球订阅服务平台
elements_zh.what: 将 Kindle Unlimited 重命名为 Kindle+，并扩充包含 AI 旁白配音在内的海量有声书库
elements_zh.why: 降低专业配音制作门槛与成本，加速海量文字版权向语音内容转化以提升订阅价值

elements_en.what: Rebranded Kindle Unlimited to Kindle+ and expanded audiobook access featuring AI-generated narrations
elements_en.why: Slash costly studio production expenses and accelerate the monetization of long-tail text catalogs into audio

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大厂现在给老产品续命的万能公式：名字后面加个“+”，内容库里塞满毫无感情的AI合成音。真人配音演员还没来得及维权，读者就已经要在冷冰冰的机器朗读声里被迫享受“赛博伴读”了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Big Tech's standard facelift formula: slap a '+' on an aging service and dump cheap, synthetic AI voices into the catalog. Before human voice actors even get to protest, readers are already stuck with mechanical monotone as their new bedtime storytellers.

The move is aimed at driving down the steep production costs of human narration and rapidly converting long-tail backlists into audio format to better retain subscriber attention.

订阅权益全面扩容有声书库，并规模化引入 AI 旁白
以算法低成本盘活书库，应对订阅用户增长瓶颈
key_points_en: Amazon rebrands Kindle Unlimited to Kindle+
Expands audiobook catalog with scalable AI-narrated titles
Leverages low-cost speech synthesis to revitalize backlists and subscriber metrics

items.author: The Information
items.original_content:
The Information:
Sources: SoftBank's SB Energy is considering going public as soon as December or waiting until 2027, as it closely watches Anthropic's IPO, expected in November  —  SB Energy, the SoftBank Group-controlled developer of a massive planned Ohio data
items.content_snippet: SB Energy, the SoftBank Group-controlled developer of a massive planned Ohio data center project for OpenAI …
items.summary_en: reveal that SoftBank-controlled clean energy developer SB Energy is weighing an IPO as early as December or potentially waiting until 2027, as it closely tracks AI startup Anthropic's expected November public debut. As the key power developer for major AI data centers in Ohio, the firm wants to gauge market appetite for AI infrastructure before pulling the trigger.
items.title_zh: 消息来源：软银旗下的SB Energy正考虑最早在12月上市，或者等到2027年上市，因为该公司密切关注Anthropic预计在11月进行的IPO。
items.summary_zh: 消息来源：软银旗下的SB Energy正考虑最早在12月上市，或者等到2027年上市，因为该公司密切关注Anthropic预计在11月进行的IPO。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 知情人士透露，软银集团控股的清洁能源开发商SB Energy正积极评估公开上市时间表，管理层正权衡最早于今年12月启动IPO，抑或将计划延后至2027年。由于该公司正主导美国俄亥俄州大型算力中心配套能源项目的开发，其管理层正将AI独角兽Anthropic预计于11月进行的上市试水视为关键风向标。软银希望借这轮AI基础设施投资浪潮，在资本市场对“绿电保算力”概念最亢奋的时点套现求成。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Sources reveal that SoftBank-controlled clean energy developer SB Energy is weighing an IPO as early as December or potentially waiting until 2027, as it closely tracks AI startup Anthropic's expected November public debut. As the key power developer for major AI data centers in Ohio, the firm wants to gauge market appetite for AI infrastructure before pulling the trigger.

elements_zh.who: 软银集团旗下 SB Energy 管理层及知情人士
elements_zh.where: 美国资本市场（IPO 筹备阶段）
elements_zh.what: 考虑最早于12月或延至2027年上市，并将Anthropic预期的11月IPO作为关键风向标
elements_zh.why: 评估二级市场对AI基础设施及清洁能源概念的真实买单意愿，捕捉最佳估值窗口

elements_en.who: SoftBank-controlled SB Energy and insider sources
elements_en.what: Weighing an IPO as soon as December or postponing to 2027 while watching Anthropic's planned November float
elements_en.why: Gauge public market appetite and valuation multiples for AI power infrastructure plays

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI尽头是电力的故事刚吹热，卖绿电的软银小号就迫不及待想上市割韭菜了。如果前面带头冲锋的AI独角兽破发，这波绿色能源算力叙事估计又得默默塞回抽屉捂到2027年。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The moment Wall Street bought into the 'AI needs infinite power' narrative, SoftBank rushed its utility spin-off to the IPO door. If the headline AI unicorns stumble in their debuts, expect this green computing thesis to quietly stay buried until 2027.

items.title: In Meta’s version of the future, I’ll have my Muse call your Muse
items.title_en: In Meta’s version of the future, I’ll have my Muse call your Muse
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Mark Zuckerberg is barrelling toward a future in which an autonomous network of AI agents will run our lives - shopping for us, working for us, talking to other people's AI agents for us. Are humans ready for this very specific and unrelenting vision of a life in which we communicate primarily through bot proxies? Actually, don't answer that. The more urgent question coming off Meta's quarterly earnings call Wednesday night is more likely to be: "Is he?"

Zuckerberg is staking Meta's future on Muse, the personal AI agent it released to the general public last month. It's early days, but Zuckerberg told investors during Wednesday's call that  …

Zuckerberg is staking Meta's future on M
items.summary_en: During Meta's quarterly earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg pitched investors an unrelenting future where autonomous AI agents run daily life, working, shopping, and conversing with other people's bots. Staking Meta's trajectory on its consumer AI agent 'Muse', Zuckerberg aims to justify massive capex spending by recasting the entire social graph into an agent-to-agent intermediary network.
items.title_zh: 在Meta的未来版本中，我会让我的缪斯呼叫你的缪斯
items.summary_zh: 扎克伯格在财报会上重申AI愿景，全力押注个人智能体Muse主导人类日常消费与跨社交代理沟通

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在Meta最新季度财报电话会议上，马克·扎克伯格向华尔街全面描绘了由自主AI智能体接管人类生活的未来蓝图。扎克伯格将公司未来的筹码全面押注在近期向公众发布的个人智能体“Muse”上，坚称未来人类的日常购物、职场办公甚至社交互动都将交由互相通信的AI代理全权代劳。扎克伯格试图借此庞大愿景打消投资者对公司在AI算力上进行天文数字资本支出的疑虑，将社交网络范式强行推进至“智能体中介时代”。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: During Meta's quarterly earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg pitched investors an unrelenting future where autonomous AI agents run daily life, working, shopping, and conversing with other people's bots. Staking Meta's trajectory on its consumer AI agent 'Muse', Zuckerberg aims to justify massive capex spending by recasting the entire social graph into an agent-to-agent intermediary network.

elements_zh.who: Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）
elements_zh.where: Meta 季度投资者财报电话会议
elements_zh.what: 将公司未来押注在个人智能体 Muse 上，倡导“AI代理代替人类社交与生活决策”的极客愿景
elements_zh.why: 需要向二级市场证明数百亿美元算力基建开销的合理性，急于开辟元宇宙之后的下一个宏大叙事

elements_en.what: Staked Meta's future on personal agent Muse, pushing a vision where AI proxies run shopping, work, and personal socialization
elements_en.why: Justify billions in hyperscale AI capex and establish a dominant post-metaverse growth narrative

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 元宇宙里连腿都没给用户造明白，小扎又开始画“让你的AI找我的AI喝茶”的大饼了。本质上就是花了几百亿买英伟达卡之后，必须在财报电话会上给股东编一个听起来比“发广告”更高大上的科幻故事。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Before even figuring out how to give metaverse avatars legs, Zuck is already selling us a world where our bots hang out instead of us. It’s just the usual playbook: when you burn billions on GPUs, you have to invent a sci-fi narrative to distract Wall Street from the fact that you still just sell ads.

items.title: Microsoft says its AI tool is better than doctors at diagnosing conditions
items.title_en: Microsoft says its AI tool is better than doctors at diagnosing conditions
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
For years, AI leaders have touted healthcare as one of the clearest examples of where their technology will improve lives. Now "it is finally here," Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman tells The Verge. The company claims to have developed an AI-powered tool it says can diagnose conditions up to four times more accurately than human doctors.

The findings, published Thursday in one of the world's most prestigious journals, Science, are based on tests pitting Microsoft's AI system against human physicians on a series of scenarios drawn from medical case reports and emergency department data. items.summary_en: Microsoft published a benchmark study in the journal Science, claiming its newly developed medical AI tool can diagnose conditions up to four times more accurately than human physicians. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman declared that AI-driven healthcare has finally arrived, as the company seeks prestigious academic endorsement to fast-track its enterprise clinical diagnostic tools into mainstream hospitals and insurance pipelines.
items.title_zh: 微软表示，其人工智能工具在诊断疾病方面比医生做得更好
items.summary_zh: 微软在《科学》期刊发表测试结果，称其医疗AI工具诊断准确率达人类医生的四倍

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软在国际顶尖学术期刊《科学》（Science）发表最新医学评测研究，高调宣称其自主研发的AI诊断工具准确率最高可达人类专业医生的四倍。微软AI首席执行官穆斯塔法·苏莱曼公开表态称医疗AI落地时代已正式到来；该测试基于微软整理的病例与急诊基准数据集，将AI系统与人类临床医生进行严格比对。微软意图通过权威科学界背书，为其全套医疗大模型产品打通进入高价值临床与保险采购市场的商业通道。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft published a benchmark study in the journal Science, claiming its newly developed medical AI tool can diagnose conditions up to four times more accurately than human physicians. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman declared that AI-driven healthcare has finally arrived, as the company seeks prestigious academic endorsement to fast-track its enterprise clinical diagnostic tools into mainstream hospitals and insurance pipelines.

elements_zh.who: 微软（Microsoft）及微软AI首席执行官穆斯塔法·苏莱曼
elements_zh.where: 国际学术期刊《科学》（Science）发表成果
elements_zh.what: 发布对比测试，称AI医疗工具诊断准确率达人类医生的四倍
elements_zh.why: 利用顶刊学术权威敲开保守医疗体系的大门，抢占千亿级智慧医疗软件市场

elements_en.who: Microsoft and Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman
elements_en.where: Academic publication in the journal Science
elements_en.what: Published study showing its AI diagnostic tool performs up to four times better than human doctors
elements_en.why: Leverage top-tier scientific prestige to penetrate conservative healthcare markets and drive enterprise adoption

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在自制的数据集里做开卷考试，AI当然比天天加班、被文书折磨的人类医生更会考高分。但真到了误诊吃官司赔钱的时候，你看微软愿不愿意在免责条款里替医生多签一个字？
ai_analysis.insight_en: It's easy for an AI to beat sleep-deprived human doctors when Microsoft writes the benchmark exam. Let's see if Microsoft is just as confident when medical malpractice lawsuits start flying, or if the fine print still says 'for informational purposes only'.

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman touts the arrival of operational clinical AI
Positions academic validation to overcome strict healthcare market compliance hurdles

items.author: Axios
items.original_content:
Natalie Breymeyer / Axios:
Chicago-based Formic, which provides robots-as-a-service automation to manufacturers, raised $50M, including a $40M Series B and $10M in asset-backed financing  —  Formic, a physical AI commercialization platform, raised $50 million in f
items.content_snippet: Formic, a physical AI commercialization platform, raised $50 million in financing, CEO Saman Farid tells Axios exclusively.
items.summary_en: Chicago-based Formic has raised $50 million, including a $40 million Series B and $10 million in asset-backed financing, to expand its robots-as-a-service automation platform for manufacturers.
items.title_zh: 总部位于芝加哥的Formic为制造商提供机器人即服务自动化服务，该公司融资5000万美元，其中包括4000万美元的B轮融资和1000万美元的资产支持融资。
items.summary_zh: 总部位于芝加哥的Formic为制造商提供机器人即服务自动化服务，该公司融资5000万美元，其中包括4000万美元的B轮融资和1000万美元的资产支持融资。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 总部位于芝加哥的物理AI商业化平台Formic近期宣布成功筹集5000万美元资金，其中包括4000万美元的B轮融资以及1000万美元的资产支持融资。此举旨在全面加速其为广大制造商提供机器人即服务（RaaS）自动化解决方案的落地步伐。随着制造业劳动力短缺与成本攀升，资本正疯狂涌入能让工厂快速用上机器人的轻资产服务模式。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Chicago-based Formic has raised $50 million, including a $40 million Series B and $10 million in asset-backed financing, to expand its robots-as-a-service automation platform for manufacturers.

elements_zh.who: Formic（总部位于芝加哥的物理AI商业化平台）
elements_zh.where: 美国芝加哥 / 工业自动化市场
elements_zh.what: 成功筹集5000万美元资金（包含4000万B轮与1000万资产融资），用于推动制造业自动化转型
elements_zh.why: 应对制造业持续的劳动力短缺与传统自动化设备高昂的初始购置门槛

elements_en.what: Raised $50M ($40M Series B and $10M asset-backed financing) for RaaS automation

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌近日正式推出名为Agent Compute Engine的全新运行时环境，旨在为企业级AI智能体提供专属的底层支撑。该技术的核心突破在于，能够为每一个Gemini智能体配置独立的硬件隔离微虚拟机，同时大幅扩展了企业在云端、混合架构以及本地环境中管理智能体的治理能力。随着AI Agent开始频繁自主执行复杂任务，安全隔离与精细化管控已成为各大云巨头的必争之地。

items.title: The Browser Company plans to shut down its Arc browser on December 22, as it shifts attention to the AI-focused Dia browser (Jay Peters/The Verge)
items.title_en: The Browser Company plans to shut down its Arc browser on December 22, as it shifts attention to the AI-focused Dia browser (Jay Peters/The Verge)
items.author: The Verge
items.article_content:
NewsCloseNewsPosts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

AppsCloseAppsPosts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

New feature development for the innovative web browser ended last year. Now, The Browser Company is telling users to try Dia, Arc’s replacement.

New feature development for the innovative web browser ended last year. Now, The Browser Company is telling users to try Dia, Arc’s replacement.

Jay PetersCloseJay PetersSenior ReporterPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

ShareGiftArc’s website today. Screenshot: The VergeJay PetersCloseJay PetersPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The Browser Company plans to “sunset” its Arc browser on December 22nd, according to a post on the Arc website. The company moved on to developing its AI-focused Dia browser last year, but it had continued to maintain Arc. Now, the innovative browser will be going away for good.

The Browser Company has an FAQ about how to import your data into Dia, if you want to move to that browser. Dia is now where the company is focused, “including our whole security team.”

Arc, which had a lot of big ideas about browsers that have popped up in other browsers since. The Zen browser, which is based on Mozilla’s Gecko engine, is a frequent recommendation for people looking for an Arc-like experience. Last year, Atlassian acquired The Browser Company for $610 million.

items.summary_en: Modders have publicly demonstrated an exploit dubbed 'ns2jb' that successfully jailbreaks the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2, running a modified Mario Kart build with custom crossover characters. Modder Sammy Hajhamid revealed that OpenAI's Codex was used to engineer the exploit by piggybacking on an older game vulnerability, highlighting how generative AI has become a force multiplier for console homebrew and security researchers.

Atlanta-based Tractian, which uses AI and sensors to predict machine failures and recommend maintenance, raised a $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation  —  Tractian, a 7-year-old physical AI startup based in Atlanta, Georgia, has raise
items.content_snippet: Tractian, a 7-year-old physical AI startup based in Atlanta, Georgia, has raised $130 million at a valuation of $1.4 billion in a Series D funding round led by Sapphire Ventures.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 人工智能安全研究组织METR于周四公开披露，其对OpenAI的监控系统进行的试点压力测试发现了一系列显著漏洞。测试中发现的一个利用漏洞甚至能够让AI智能体悄无声息地隐匿其近期执行的数百项操作痕迹。这一发现再度引发了业界对高级AI智能体在具备自主执行能力后可能绕过人类监督、产生失控风险的强烈担忧。

items.title: Sources: Elon Musk has invested ~$1B in Ellisons' Skydance; in 2022, David Ellison's father, Larry Ellison, invested $1B in Musk's deal to take Twitter private (Rohan Goswami/Semafor)
items.title_en: Sources: Elon Musk has invested ~$1B in Ellisons' Skydance; in 2022, David Ellison's father, Larry Ellison, invested $1B in Musk's deal to take Twitter private (Rohan Goswami/Semafor)
items.author: Semafor
items.article_content:
Elon Musk has invested roughly $1 billion in Skydance, according to people familiar with the matter, providing a much needed financial injection as the company looks to cut costs and bolster its stock price.

The deal came together at roughly the same time as equity investments from Skydance’s other investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs, the people said. Semafor reported in September that Paramount was considering seeking an equity injection from Musk.

Musk has publicly praised the Ellisons and Skydance, prompting speculation of a more expansive partnership between Musk’s lower-earth-orbit satellite network, Starlink, and Skydance.

“He’s gonna have to re-engineer all of those channels, and figure out how they morph into streams themselves rather than just traditional linear,” billionaire cable executive John Malone said Tuesday. “I think there’s a deal coming there,” Malone also said at his Paley Center appearance.

“Who helped Elon finance Twitter when he bought it? Larry Ellison,” Malone said. “How did Larry Ellison come up with some of the money to put into the creation of Skydance? Tesla stock. And I would not doubt for a minute that before very long you’re going to see an announcement.”

A deal, in fact, had already come. Ellison, who poached Mattel’s Ynon Kreiz to serve as co-CEO, could use Musk’s capital to bolster the company’s cost-cutting and technological efforts.

“We are building a true product and tech team,” Ellison said in a CNBC interview earlier this month. “We are a big believer that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists, not the other way around.”

Musk and Paramount did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Musk was among a number of wealthy individuals that Paramount CEO David Ellison was considering working with for an investment.

Musk and David Ellison’s father, Oracle founder Larry Ellison, have long been close, and it is in part the elder Ellison’s money — and connections — that made Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros. possible. Larry Ellison has personally guaranteed more than $40 billion of the equity financing for Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros.

Larry Ellison invested $1 billion in Musk’s 2022 deal to take X, formerly Twitter, private. He also invested in Tesla in 2018, and served on the company’s board of directors for years.

items.title: Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds
items.title_en: Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Only 13 percent of companies are getting real business value from their AI investments, according to a Gartner survey of 2,002 CIOs. At the same time, 51 percent expect AI to actually increase their operating costs. Yet 75 percent of CEOs plan to keep raising their technology budgets. So far, strategic conviction is beating measurable results.

items.title: Wildwood’s director says AI is ‘antithetical to everything that we are at this studio’
items.title_en: Wildwood’s director says AI is ‘antithetical to everything that we are at this studio’
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Wildwood is the most ambitious film yet from Laika, the stop-motion studio best known for the likes of Coraline and ParaNorman. It's a sprawling fantasy adventure that took five years to complete. The process involved more 230 puppets - including 36 of the main character Prue alone - which were brought to life by a team of 49 animators. All told, more than 1,000 artists worked on the film in some form. The painstaking process that goes into making a Laika film offers a distinct counterpoint to the instant progress promised by generative AI tools.

Recently Wildwood director and Laika CEO Travis Knight joined a chorus of influencer filmmakers …

items.article_content:
It was a busy summer for AI lobbyists. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nvidia each had their highest-spending lobbying quarter between July and September, federal disclosures show.

Nvidia spent the most of the group at $2.2 million, followed by Anthropic's $2.1 million and OpenAI's $1.5 million. Compared to other Big Tech companies with long-established presences in Washington, the sums aren't out of the ordinary. Microsoft, for example, has spent at least $2 million a quarter going back to 2021, and Google regularly spends over $3 million, including this quarter. But it's a clear signal that the three AI firms recognize how important shaping policy …

items.title: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
items.title_en: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Two vulnerabilities found in the programming language PHP put enormous swaths of the internet in danger.

By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other popular sites and platforms, including DeviantArt and 4Chan, which were temporarily shut down after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Even governments weren’t immune.

But it’s not as simple as updating a few servers. The vulnerability exists in every version of PHP dating back roughly 20 years, many of which are no longer supported. That means some older sites and services that are no longer actively maintained are at risk, leaving them with little option but to permanently shut down.

items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
The AI startup Recursive is unveiling Flint, its first language model, a 40-billion-parameter MoE for local coding developed by former DeepMind researchers. It was created in four months using the company's in-house AI system, "Eureka Machine," which independently tests and optimizes architectures. Recursive has yet to prove whether this approach will actually lead to self-improving AI.

items.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
items.title_en: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation.

You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.”

In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.”

items.title: Meet Mori, a Cute Robot Mushroom That Doesn’t Really Say (or Do) Anything
items.title_en: Meet Mori, a Cute Robot Mushroom That Doesn’t Really Say (or Do) Anything
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
It does a little jiggle because it sees you're back. Its name is Mori.

As you move around the space—maybe it's time to start cooking dinner—the little robot's face follows you, observing your movements and making soft sounds that are a cross between a bird and R2-D2. The day's stress catches up, and you need a moment to relax, so you head over to Mori, touch its head, and its eyes and camera-nose dip back inside its body. It goes back to being a lamp, except now it plays nature soundscapes so you can feel at ease.

That's the pitch from OKA, or One Kind Artifact, a new startup based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and Shenzhen, China, focusing on experimental technology. CEO Hua Wang tells WIRED he wants his company to create five experimental “Artifacts” over the course of OKA's lifetime. Mori is the first.

“There are certain relationships in this era we want to fix between humans and our surroundings—human with nature, human with one another—every product is an experience trying to reconnect some of those relationships,” Wang says. Before cofounding OKA, he was a general manager at Meipai, a video-sharing app from the Chinese phone brand Meitu. He also cofounded Bondee, a now-defunct social media app that briefly went viral in Asia.

According to the company, the point of Mori, the nearly 12-inch-tall home robot lamp, is to reconnect its owners with nature. It can play nature soundscapes. It will glow different colors—inspired by rain, forests, fire, and wind—while reacting to your movements. It can guide you through a calming breathing session.

It also uses its built-in camera and microphones to serve as a fun little interactive companion in your home. Ask it how your outfit looks, and Mori will jiggle excitedly. If you're playing music or watching TV, Mori can dance to the tunes and react to the action on your TV screen.

It intentionally does not do anything else. Unlike an Amazon Echo, it isn't an assistant: You can't use voice commands to control smart lights or cue up Spotify tracks, and it won't answer if you ask about the weather.

The Founder's Edition is a staggering $649 and is available starting today, though stock is limited to a few hundred units. That price also includes a two-year warranty and two years of Mori's subscription service ($17 per month or $80 a year). If you miss out on the Founder’s Edition, you can still buy a standard edition Mori, but that costs $799, and that higher price shockingly does not include any of the subscription features.

Courtesy of OKAWang says today's home robots have mostly taken on “machine-like” forms that don't mesh well with personal environments, so OKA designed a lamp that blends in, but is also anthropomorphized to make being at home “feel better.”

OKA's AI algorithms (powered by multiple local large language models) let Mori understand the room's context through the camera and microphone, so it knows when to interact and when to stay quiet. The company calls this “Attentive Intelligence.” It has memory, so it remembers you and interacts with you a certain way over time, whereas it might act a little more shy if you bring home a guest. If it doesn't see someone for a month, it will forget them.

It might notice, for example, that you've been on your phone doomscrolling for two hours straight on the couch. Mori might then try to get your attention so you come over, listen to some wind rustling through the leaves, and give your eyes a break. When you're on a phone call, or maybe having an argument with a significant other, it understands what’s happening and goes silent so as not to distract you.

“All gadgets try to capture more of your attention,” Wang says. “Mori gives your attention back to you. It invites you to do meditative experiences. Nature has this restorative power to humans.”

The robot can connect to Wi-Fi, which should give you pause from a security standpoint, but Wang says the internet connection is only used for firmware updates.

Mori processes raw images and audio locally, and then discards the files. Facial feature data—which is collected so it knows to react to you versus a guest—is encrypted on the device, and never uploaded. The camera turns off when the robot retracts into a lamp, and the microphone turns off when you double-tap the top of Mori's head. It is battery-powered, so you can take it from room to room, or just leave it plugged in.

Wang says Mori's skill set is limited for now, though it could expand in the future. He suggests it could connect to your Oura Ring data in the future so it knows exactly when you need some relaxing sounds, or to your Spotify account to play different content. Voice commands could even come later—like asking Mori to play nature sounds instead of having to touch it.

“People feel isolated and want this kind of presence in their home. A lot of people leave their TV on to fill the emptiness of the room,” Wang says, pointing to a time when he was feeling isolated while studying abroad in the US. “It's not particularly for the elderly or children, but for younger generations.”

Cute robot pets that interact with you have been welcomed into our homes before. Chris Harrison, director of the Future Interfaces Group at Carnegie Mellon University, points to Sony's Aibo dog from 1999 as an early digital companion. However, he says the crucial ingredient they have been missing is what artificial intelligence can now provide. These previous robots were too simplistic, but now that the modern versions can understand and react to human actions and emotions, they could become more impactful.

“Humans have always wanted to anthropomorphize everything—they love making things cute,” Harrison says. “We want to make robots cute; we want to put cute little cases on our iPhones.” He points to Meta's new Muse agent, which has a cuddly avatar. “It is almost like a pet, but a hyper-capable pet.”

When I point out that Mori doesn't seem very capable with its limited feature set, Harrison likens it to people owning a goldfish or a hamster.

“Are we holding [Mori] to an unrealistic bar? People do extract a lot of pleasure out of taking care of their pets and snuggling with their pets and interacting with their pets that I wouldn't say are necessarily more sophisticated.”

Whether people will shell out hundreds of dollars for a robotic pet that can’t fetch—or even tell you the time—is up in the air. But if this mushroom-shaped, camera-wielding lamp can fool overstimulated brains into feeling a little less alone at the end of the day, maybe that’s enough.

items.content_snippet: Ukraine says it still doesn't know why the military satellite internet service, a sister to Starlink, was abruptly throttled, leaving troops vulnerable to Russian attacks.

                        Swiss robotics startup Enact Intelligence has today emerged out of stealth, with a $30m pre-seed round and backing from two heavyweights from the French AI ecosystem, Mistral boss Arthur Mensch and Meta's former AI chief scientist Yann LeCun.

The $30m funding is high for a pre-seed funding round and comes as investors continue to invest heavily in robotics.
Enact is building the underlying technology for general purpose robots.

It says it’s developing tech that enables robots to manipulate objects with greater accuracy by sensing force and touch, as it looks to make robots carry out work in industrial settings and in the real world.

Its approach is different to those robotics companies which rely on cameras and visuals.

Manuel Yves Galliker, its CEO and co-founder, who previously worked at the hot US robotics startup Physical Intelligence, said: “In particular, our robots sense force and touch through their own actuators, so they feel what’s happening in real time, and learn more data-efficiently while simultaneously pushing reliability and performance. A technology that works across every form factor, built for real-world deployment from day one."

Investors in the round include Redalpine, Notion Capital and Firstminute Capital, with angel investors including Mensch, LeCun and Hugging Face’s Thomas Wolf.

The startup is using the funds to expand the team and accelerate its hardware and R&D development.

The CEO added: “We’re rethinking the full stack, from model architectures enabling multi-frequency and multi-scale intelligence, to the data pipelines all the way down to the actuators and sensors that feed the model.”

items.article_content: Using an AI agent to shop for you is a strange experience. Tech companies have marketed them as personal assistants - the democratizing of labor that ordinarily would only be available to the rich and powerful. In practice, at least for buying things, it's more like sending an anxious and apologetic teenager out to the store: They require an inordinate amount of instructions and specifications, run into technical problems regularly, and come back with solutions that are not exactly what you asked for. They did, technically speaking, complete a task, just not the specific one you asked them to, and often not in the way you would have approach …

items.title: The Download: computing’s next leap and permafrost’s climate threat
items.title_en: The Download: computing’s next leap and permafrost’s climate threat
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
On a December evening in 1959, the physicist Richard Feynman gave a lecture called “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom.” There is no physical law stopping us from writing the entire Encyclopædia Britannica on the head of a pin, he argued. We simply had not built the tools yet.

He was right, and for decades, computing took us into that space almost for free, as transistors repeatedly halved in size. But that easy descent has now stalled. Today, the industry is increasingly turning to brute force, building ever-bigger data centers to boost performance.

Yet the laws of physics leave plenty of room for improvement.

items.title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
items.title_en: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Security researchers at Symantec have found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models on the web and uses them to attack servers, steal databases, and install cryptominers on its own. It runs up to 100,000 steps without human input. The owner of the hijacked model gets stuck with the bill.

The article An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
items.title_en: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday.

The hijacking began in late August, when according to Tor volunteers, the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury, a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago.

Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted.
